I:1-2:
The Zohar opens. R. Chizkiyah begins from “as a rose among the thorns”: the rose is Knesset Yisrael, red and white in her as judgment and mercy are; thirteen petals to her as thirteen attributes of mercy surround her, and thirteen words stand between the first אֱלֹהִים of the account and the next, set there to encircle her and keep her. Five strong leaves hold her up — five gates of salvation, the כּוֹס יְשׁוּעוֹת — which is why the cup of blessing is carried on five fingers and no more.

R. Shimon reads the days of creation out of “the blossoms appeared in the land”: the third day when the earth brought forth, the fourth with its זְמִיר עָרִיצִים, the fifth with the voice of the turtledove, the sixth with “let us make man” — doing set before hearing, as Israel would set it — and “in our land” the Shabbat. Read again, the blossoms are the Patriarchs: they entered thought, were hidden in the world to come, were concealed in the prophets, were born in Yosef and planted by him in the Holy Land. What holds the world up meanwhile, and what brings them out, is the voice of children learning Torah.

Then R. Eleazar on “lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these.” מִי is the hidden one that stands open to the question and is never answered, the end of heaven above; מַה is below, where a man who has searched from rung to rung arrives and is asked back — what have you known, what have you seen? — and finds it all sealed as at the start. Jacob inherits both, the bar that reaches from end to end.

R. Shimon tells him to stop, and weeps, and tells what was given him once on the seashore. Eliyahu asked him what מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה is, and then told him: when the most hidden of all wished to be revealed it made first a single point, and the point rose to be thought, and in thought it engraved every form. What it engraved there is called מִי, the beginning of the building — standing and not standing, too deep to be named anything else. Wishing to be named, it clothed itself in a garment of splendour and created אֵלֶּה, and the letters joined and completed אֱלֹהִים. Until it created אֵלֶּה that name did not rise — and it is the same word the makers of the calf took when they said אֵלֶּה אֱלֹהֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל, the letters torn from what joins them. Eliyahu flew, and he saw him no more. The companions fell before him weeping: had we come into the world only to hear this, it would be enough.

The folio closes with Rav Hamnuna Saba and the letters, each coming before the Holy One from the end of the alphabet to ask that the world be made with her. Tav is the seal of truth and is refused, being also the seal of death; Shin is true, but ק”ר take hold of her to stand their falsehood up — which is how a lie is built, a true thing taken first.
I:11-12:
Sarah nursed their sons before them and said צְחֹק עָשָׂה לִי אֱלֹהִים, and the accuser was still at the door. He went up at once: You called Avraham Your beloved — he made a feast and gave You nothing and the poor nothing, not so much as a dove; and Sarah laughed. Who in the world is like Avraham, said the Holy One. But he did not move until he had confounded all that rejoicing: it was then that Yitzchak was called for as an offering, and decreed that Sarah should die of grief for her son. All that grief came of one thing — that nothing had been given to the poor.

R. Shimon opens on וַיַּסֵּב חִזְקִיָּהוּ פָּנָיו אֶל הַקִּיר: whoever labours in the Torah fears neither those above nor below nor the evil sicknesses of the world, for he holds to the Tree of Life. She gives him counsel how to turn back and annul a decree — even one decreed not to be annulled is lifted from him at once. Hence וְהָגִיתָ בּוֹ יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה, for whoever parts from her has parted from the Tree of Life. Going up on his bed at night let him take the kingdom above upon himself and give over the deposit of his soul, and he is saved from every evil spirit; and rising, let him bless his Master and bow before His palace in fear and take counsel of the fathers — בְּרֹב חַסְדְּךָ Avraham, אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶה אֶל הֵיכַל קָדְשְׁךָ Yitzchak, בְּיִרְאָתֶךָ Yaakov — including them first, and only then entering to pray.

R. Pinchas was with R. Rechumai by the sea of Ginnosar, an old man whose eyes had failed. I have heard that Yochai our colleague has a pearl, he said; I looked into its light and it came out like the sun from its sheath and lit the whole world, standing from heaven to earth until the Ancient of Days should sit upon His throne — and all that light is gathered in your house, and out of it a thin small light goes out and lights the world. Go after that pearl, my son; the hour stands for you. He went, and seeing two birds over the sea called out: birds, have you seen where bar Yochai is? Go and bring me an answer. They flew out and were gone, and came back with a note in the mouth of one: bar Yochai has come out of the cave, he and his son. He found him changed, his body full of sores, and wept — woe that I see you so. Happy is my portion, said R. Shimon, that you see me so; had you not, I would not be so.

Then the commandments. The first of all is the fear of the Lord, called רֵאשִׁית — the gate by which one enters faith, and the world stands on it. Fear divides three ways and two have no root: the man who fears so that his children may live, or for his body or his money; and the man who fears the punishment of that world and of Gehinnom. The root is that a man fear his Master because He is great and rules, the foundation of all the worlds, and all before Him are as nothing.

R. Shimon wept: woe if I say it and woe if I do not — if I say it the wicked will know how to serve their Master, and if I do not the companions will lose it. Below the place of holy fear is an evil fear that strikes and accuses, a strap for beating the wicked; and the man who fears the strap does not have יִרְאַת יְיָ לְחַיִּים upon him but that other. Whoever keeps fear keeps everything and whoever does not keeps nothing, since this is the gate of all: בְּרֵאשִׁית, which is fear, בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים — and whoever passes it meets the four punishments written in one verse, תֹהוּ strangling, בֹהוּ the stoning-stones sunk in the great deep, חֹשֶׁךְ burning, and רוּחַ the sword, לַהַט הַחֶרֶב הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת.

The second is bound to it and never departs from it: to love one's Master with whole love, אַהֲבָה רַבָּה — הִתְהַלֵּךְ לְפָנַי וֶהְיֵה תָמִים, which is יְהִי אוֹר. R. Eleazar says it before R. Pinchas, who stands in that rung: love is whole only on two sides. One who loves Him for his wealth and length of days and children, and would hate Him if the wheel of hard judgement turned on him, has a love with no root. Whole love holds in judgement as in kindness — even if He takes your soul from you. So the light of creation came out and was hidden, and when it was hidden hard judgement came out, and the two were gathered into one.

R. Shimon kissed him, and R. Pinchas kissed him and blessed him: surely the Holy One sent me here — this is the thin light they told me of. And fear must not be forgotten in any commandment, least of all this one. On the good side a man must rouse fear lest sin end it, אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד; and seeing hard judgement rest on him he must rouse fear and not harden his heart, וּמַקְשֶׁה לִבּוֹ יִפּוֹל בְּרָעָה. Fear held to both sides is whole love.

The third: to know there is a great God who rules the world and to unify Him each day in the six supernal sides, made one in the six words of שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל — which is why אֶחָד is drawn out the length of six words. יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם is the rungs beneath heaven gathering to be one in Him; and fear is bound in, which is why the ד of אֶחָד is written large — וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה. Then it is bound below with its hosts in six other words, בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ, and the dry land becomes earth and bears fruit. Hence כִּי טוֹב twice: the unification above and the one below.

The fourth: to know that יְיָ הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים, including the one name in the other with no parting — black light in white light, the cloud of day and the cloud of fire by night, each set right by the other. This was the first serpent's sin: he joined below and parted above, where a man must part below and join above. Which is the secret of מְאֹרֹת written short: the brain is אוֹר and the other side מָוֶת — light in the joining of the letters, death in their parting. From those letters Chava began, וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה כִּי טוֹב: turn them and מ״ו is left, and the ו that is always life turned and took the ת with it — וַתִּקַּח וַתִּתֵּן — and brought death into the world.

The fifth and sixth are both in יִשְׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה: to labour in the Torah, to be fruitful and multiply, and to circumcise on the eighth day. Whoever labours in her is set right with another holy soul, the soul of that holy Chayah, and comes to be like the holy angels — בָּרְכוּ יְיָ מַלְאָכָיו, His angels on earth; and in that world He will make them wings like eagles. And whoever is fruitful and multiplies causes that river to flow unceasing and new souls to be renewed out of the tree. With every soul that comes into this world two birds come out of the tree with it, one from the right and one from the left: if he merits they guard him, כִּי מַלְאָכָיו יְצַוֶּה לָּךְ — and if not, they are his accusers.
I:13-16:
Three stand guardian over a man when he merits, read out of אִם יֵשׁ עָלָיו מַלְאָךְ מֵלִיץ אֶחָד מִנִּי אֶלֶף — and R. Shimon counts five, until he is told that וַיְחֻנֶּנּוּ is the Holy One alone, for none other has that authority. Well said, he answers. And whoever holds back from being fruitful lessens, as it were, the image that holds all images, and stops that river from flowing, and blemishes the covenant on every side.

The seventh commandment is to circumcise on the eighth day and take away the filth of the foreskin — for that Chayah is the eighth of all the rungs, and the soul that flies from her must be seen before her on the eighth day, as she herself is eighth. Then it is truly נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, the soul of that holy Chayah and not of the other side. The book of Chanoch has it that the waters of holy seed are marked with the mark of a living soul — the letter יוֹד cut into holy flesh, above every other mark in the world. And וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף עַל הָאָרֶץ is Eliyahu, who flies the whole world in four flights to be there at that circumcision; a chair must be made ready for him and named aloud, the chair of Eliyahu, or he does not rest there.

The eighth is to love the proselyte who comes to be circumcised and to enter under the wings of the Shechinah — תּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה לְמִינָהּ. Under her right wing are two chambers, and from that wing branch two nations near to Israel; under the left two more, Ammon and Moav; and in every wing further hidden chambers, from which go out the spirits of all who come to convert. They are called a living soul — but לְמִינָהּ, and they come under the wings and no further. The soul of Israel comes out of the body of that tree itself, הָעֲמוּסִים מִנִּי בָטֶן, carried in the womb and not on the wings.

The ninth is to have mercy on the poor and give them food: נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ — בְּצַלְמֵנוּ the rich and כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ the poor, for from the male side come the rich and from the female the poor; and as those two are one partnership, sparing one another and giving one to the other, so must a man be below. In the book of King Shlomo: whoever has mercy on the poor with the will of his heart, his likeness never changes from the likeness of Adam — and having it, he rules every creature of the world, וּמוֹרַאֲכֶם וְחִתְּכֶם. As long as Nevuchadnezzar was gracious to the poor his dream did not settle on him; the moment he turned a grudging eye, עוֹד מִלְּתָא בְּפֻם מַלְכָּא — and his likeness changed and he was driven out from men.

The tenth is to lay tefillin and complete oneself in the supernal likeness. רֹאשֵׁךְ עָלַיִךְ כַּכַּרְמֶל is the head-tefillin, the Name of the holy King in its letters, a portion to each: קַדֶּשׁ לִי כָל בְּכוֹר the י; וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ the ה, the palace whose womb the yod opens in fifty gates — the shofar, stopped on every side until the yod opened and sounded it and drew out a voice to bring slaves to freedom, by which Israel came out of Egypt and will come out again at the end of days; שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל the ו that takes in everything; and וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ the last ה, which gathers both sides into itself. וְדַלַּת רֹאשֵׁךְ is the hand-tefillin, poor beside what is above and yet whole in the same manner — head and hand, male and female, and all one.

The eleventh is to tithe the earth and the twelfth to bring the first fruits of the tree, both in הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם — to you, and not to the generations after you. The thirteenth is to redeem one's son and bind him to life: two are appointed over a man, one of life and one of death, and in redeeming his son he redeems him from the hand of that one, who can no longer rule him — וְהִנֵּה טוֹב the angel of life and מְאֹד the angel of death.

The fourteenth is to keep the Sabbath and to sanctify it. When the day was sanctified there were left spirits for whom no bodies had been made. Did He not know to hold back until their bodies were made? Rather the tree of knowledge roused the other side, which sought to take hold in the world, and many spirits spread out armed to take bodies. Seeing it, He roused a breath out of the Tree of Life and struck the other tree and roused the side of good, and the day was sanctified — for the making of bodies on the side of good belongs to this night. Had the other side come first, the world could not have stood before them a moment; the remedy was brought first, the sanctity of the day leaping ahead of it. That is why the wise who know this keep their time from Sabbath to Sabbath.

Seeing what the side of holiness had made of its plan, the other side goes roving with its hosts, and looks for those who couple with their bodies uncovered by lamplight; and the children born of that are the ones on whom its spirits rest. Once the day is sanctified it makes itself small and hides all the night and day of Sabbath, but for Asimon and his company, who go along the lamps in hiding to see what is uncovered, and afterwards hide in the hollow of the great deep. When the Sabbath goes out, hosts and camps fly out and rove the world — and for that the Song of Afflictions was set, that they should not rule over the holy people.

Three bring evil on themselves: one who curses himself; one who throws away bread, or crumbs with an olive's bulk in them; and one who kindles a lamp at the going out of Sabbath before Israel has finished קְדוּשָּׁא דְסִדְרָא, for he lights the fire of Gehinnom before its time, and those punished there curse him. But if he waits, those same wicked ones justify the judgement upon themselves and confirm on him every blessing the congregation says. אַשְׁרֵי מַשְׂכִּיל אֶל דָּל בְּיוֹם רָעָה יְמַלְּטֵהוּ יְיָ — why בְּיוֹם רָעָה? The day when that evil rules, to take his soul.

And then the book begins again at its beginning. At the will of the King, engravings were cut in the supernal lustre — a lamp of darkness, בּוּצִינָא דְקַרְדִּינוּתָא — and out of the sealed of the sealed, from the head of Ein Sof, came a mist within a form, set in a ring: not white, not black, not red, not green, no colour at all. Only when He measured did He make colours to shine within. Sealed within the sealed, it broke and did not break through its own air, and was not known at all — until out of the pressure of its breaking one hidden supernal point shone. Beyond that point nothing is known, and therefore it is called רֵאשִׁית, the first utterance of all.

וְהַמַּשְׂכִּילִים יַזְהִירוּ כְּזֹהַר הָרָקִיעַ. The Zohar, sealed of the sealed, struck its air and struck this point, and then רֵאשִׁית spread and made itself a palace for its glory, and sowed holy seed there — זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ מַצַּבְתָּהּ — as the silkworm wraps itself within and makes the palace that is its own praise. In this רֵאשִׁית that unknown One created that palace, and the palace is called אֱלֹהִים: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים. The first of all is named אֶהְיֶה; engraved in its sides, אֱלֹהִים; engraved in the crown, אֲשֶׁר, the hidden treasured palace — the רֹאשׁ that comes out of רֵאשִׁית.

That point sowed in the palace the secret of three points — חוֹלָם, שׁוּרֻק, חִירִק — gathered one into another into one secret: a voice going out in a single union, and with it its mate, which holds all the letters. אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם is that voice and its mate. Three rungs stand against בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים — the first secret, the sealed secret from which all spreads, and the secret that upholds everything below — and אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם is written so that male and female should not be parted. אֵת takes all the letters from first to last; add a ה and it is אַתָּה, which is why וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם. And from here on, בְּרֵאשִׁית is בָּרָא שִׁית: six sides spreading from the supernal secret, out of the first point.

The מַשְׂכִּילִים shine like the cantillation that sings: the letters and the vowels go after the marks and sway behind them like hosts behind their kings — the letters the body and the vowels the spirit, and when the melody moves they move, and when it stops they stand where they are. They are the supports of that palanquin, who look with understanding into everything it needs; and if they did not shine they could not look into it at all. And the firmament they look to is the one written of in וּדְמוּת עַל רָאשֵׁי הַחַיָּה רָקִיעַ כְּעֵין הַקֶּרַח הַנּוֹרָא: the Zohar that lights the Torah, and lights those heads of the Chayah, and does not cease.

וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ — הָיְתָה exactly, beforehand: snow within water. Filth came out of it by the force of that snow, and a strong fire struck it and there was dross, set aside and become תֹהוּ, a nest of dross; בֹהוּ is what was refined out of it, and חֹשֶׁךְ the strong fire that covers it. Then the spirit hovered and refined a fine thing out of that dross, folding and purifying once and twice until what remained had no filth in it at all — and out of the refining came the great wind that breaks mountains, the one Eliyahu saw, and the earthquake after it, and darkness refined into fire, and the wind into קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה. תֹהוּ is a place with no colour and no form, and everything has a garment but this; בֹהוּ has shape — stones sunk in that engraving, pierced and moist, hanging in the air and drawing water out of the deep to feed it.

Over תֹהוּ rests the Name שַׁדַּי; over בֹהוּ, צְבָאוֹת; over חֹשֶׁךְ, אֱלֹהִים; and over רוּחַ, the Name itself. Which is why לֹא בָרוּחַ יְיָ — Shaddai rules there in the secret of תֹהוּ; לֹא בָרַעַשׁ יְיָ — Tzevaot rules in the secret of בֹהוּ, and that is why בֹהוּ is called earthquake; לֹא בָאֵשׁ יְיָ — Elohim rules from the side of darkness; and after the fire, in the still small voice, the Name is found. Four joints here, and the engraved Name of twelve letters given to Eliyahu in the cave.

וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר. From here begins the finding of what is hidden — how the world was made in particular, where until now it was in general, and afterwards returns to the general: general, particular, general. Until here all hung in the air out of the secret of Ein Sof; once the power spread into the supernal palace, saying is written of it. וַיֹּאמֶר is a power raised and raising in silence out of Ein Sof in the secret of thought — the palace now giving birth to what it had conceived of the holy seed, and giving birth in silence; and what was born was heard outside. He who bore it bore without a sound; what came out of him became a voice heard.

יְהִי is on the secret of father and mother, י״ה, returning then to the first point to begin a spreading to something else, אוֹר. And וַיְהִי אוֹר is light that already was: a spreading that broke out of the hidden supernal air, which broke first and brought out one sealed point, י — and once that yod spread, what remained was found to be light. It went out and rose and was hidden, and one point stayed of it, reaching always by way of concealment, reaching and not reaching, so that all hold one to another. That point spread, and seven letters of the alphabet shone in it and stayed moist; darkness came after it with seven more, also moist; and a firmament came out that parted the quarrel of the two sides, with eight more in it — twenty-two. The seven of each side leapt and were engraved in that firmament, and it congealed, and the letters congealed and took their shapes, and the Torah was engraved there to shine outward.

וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב is the middle pillar, which lit above and below and to every side; וַיַּבְדֵּל is that He parted the quarrel so that all should be whole. And וַיִּקְרָא is that He called and summoned: out of that whole light standing in the middle He drew one light which is the foundation of the world, on which the worlds stand — חַי עוֹלָמִים, which is day, from the right; and out of the side of darkness He called and drew one female, the moon that rules by night and is called לַיְלָה, the secret of אֲדֹנָי, אֲדוֹן כָּל הָאָרֶץ.
I:17-18:
The three points — חוֹלָם, שׁוּרֻק, חִירִק — are the holy seed. All joins in the middle pillar, which brings out the world's foundation, called כֹּל. The left blazed, and out of that blaze came the moon; the blaze was dark, being of darkness. When the middle pillar made peace on every side, light was added, and out of that added joy came מוּסָף, from which the hosts and holy souls come out.

לַיְלָה comes from the left. Darkness longed to be taken into the right, its force slackened, and night spread out of it; but the right took the darkness in before the spreading was done, and night was left wanting. As darkness longs for light, night longs for day, and what it lacks is made up only in Musaf. So the day is וַיִּקְרָא and the night קָרָא לַיְלָה, the ו״י taken from it.

יְהִי רָקִיעַ בְּתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם parts the upper waters from the lower, in the secret of the left. Until here was the right, on which all completion hangs. With the left came dispute; the fire of anger grew strong, and Gehinnom came out and fastened there. The middle pillar, the third day, came between and made the two sides agree: Gehinnom went down, the left was taken into the right, and there was peace.

Korach against Aharon was that dispute, left against right. Moshe looked into the work of creation and said: it falls to me to part right from left. The left would not agree, and Korach held to his force — Gehinnom must fasten somewhere, and he would not cling above. His dispute was not for Heaven's sake, so Moshe's hand could not reconcile it. וַיִּחַר לְמֹשֶׁה מְאֹד: וַיִּחַר that they denied him, מְאֹד that they denied creation itself.

A dispute set after the pattern above rises and does not go down: Shammai and Hillel, whom the Holy One brought to agreement, enduring because it was for Heaven's sake. Two disputes, a beginning and an end, as the righteous begin in hardship and end in rest — Korach the beginning, in anger, fastened to Gehinnom; Shammai the end, in love. וִיהִי מַבְדִּיל is the anger; וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָרָקִיעַ is the love — the Oral Torah coming to the Written, and both standing whole.

Separation belongs to the left and always to the second: בָּעֵת הַהִיא הִבְדִּיל יְיָ אֶת שֵׁבֶט הַלֵּוִי — Levi is third, but to Yaakov's mind second. So too Havdalah at the going out of Sabbath: a side comes up from Gehinnom to rule and to mix with the seed of Israel; Israel make their act with myrtle and wine, and it sinks to Sheol where Korach's company are. They go down only once Israel separate — הִבָּדְלוּ מִתּוֹךְ הָעֵדָה.

The firmament is a spreading of one from another. אֵל, the right, spread out of the waters to complete אֵל אֱלֹהִים: הַיָּם is the upper waters, and the same letters turned about are יָמָּה, the lower. Upper male, lower female; at first water within water, until they were parted and known as this אֱלֹהִים and this אֲדֹנָי, the upper ה and the lower.

Still the dispute stood until the third day, and so כִּי טוֹב is not written on the second: the work was unfinished. While the waters were together there were no offspring; once parted, they bore. The third day reconciled them, the two ה with the ו between — the sign of it the Jordan, upper waters in a heap, lower going down to the sea, Israel in the middle. Five firmaments are written here, and חַי הָעוֹלָמִים holds them one in another.

When the left was roused, the mist of the vapour thickened and hardened, and out of it came hidden ones congealed with no moisture, male and female, and evil weapons branched from them to their kinds — the unclean spirit, the secret of the foreskin. Two hold there, אֶפְעֶה and נָחָשׁ, and the two are one: the viper bears in seven years, and it returns to the serpent's seven. Hence Gehinnom has seven names, and the evil inclination seven.

יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם — by way of a line, in the way of uprightness. Out of that first point all came in concealment until it gathered into the supernal palace, then goes in a straight line to the rungs until it reaches the one place that gathers all, male and female: חַי עוֹלָמִים. מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם is the small ו, two vavs, one heaven and one beneath; and וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה is the lower ה — this one revealed, the rest covered.

אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד is the knot of the unity above, and יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד two unities, of the upper world and the lower. There all the rungs and limbs gather and are one without any parting, and nowhere else so — hence one place. שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל is the unity above, בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ the unity below.

The revealed world is unified likewise below — כְּמַרְאֵה הַקֶּשֶׁת, the secret of וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה. The bow's appearance is חַי עוֹלָמִים, and אֶת קַשְׁתִּי נָתַתִּי בֶּעָנָן is Malchut, given from the day the world was made. When the bow is seen the left is roused: Michael, Refael and Gavriel, each on his side, are its colours — white, red, green. The hidden colours above are not seen; these below are to be made one with them.

יִקָּווּ is a measuring by line, six words here and six there; the measure is בּוּצִינָא דְקַרְדִּינוּתָא — מִי מָדַד בְּשָׁעֳלוֹ מַיִם, the measure of the Former of worlds, יוּ״ד הֵ״א וָא״ו הֵ״א. קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ is יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם; יְיָ צְבָאוֹת is אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד; מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ is וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה.

תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא עֵשֶׂב — now she brings out power in those gathered waters, and holy hosts come out in her. מַצְמִיחַ חָצִיר לַבְּהֵמָה is the beast that lies on a thousand mountains, and its daily grass those angels that rule an hour, made on the second day to be its food — there is a fire that eats fire. וְעֵשֶׂב לַעֲבֹדַת הָאָדָם is the ofanim and chayot and keruvim, set in order when men come with offering and prayer, and sustenance comes out of them for the world. The grass does not seed, being food for the holy fire; the herb seeds.

עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי is rung upon rung, male and female — the keruvim, and the תִּמְרוֹת that rise in the smoke of the offering. But וּדְמוּת פְּנֵיהֶם פְּנֵי אָדָם are not the keruvim: these are great faces with a sealed beard, the keruvim small faces like children's. In the face of man all likenesses are included, engraved as the Explicit Name is engraved in the four sides of the world; and אָדָם is male and female, and is not called man but by these.
I:19-20:
The four are woven one in another — שׁוֹר, נֶשֶׁר, אַרְיֵה, אָדָם. The ox rises to look at the face of man, and a Name is crowned: אֵל; the eagle rises, גָּדוֹל; the lion, גִּבּוֹר. Man looks at them all and they all at him, and they are figured in one Name, נוֹרָא — וּדְמוּת פְּנֵיהֶם פְּנֵי אָדָם, all contained in this one likeness.

So the Holy One is called הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא, Names graven in the upper chariot and held in the four letters of יְדוָֹ״ד. The four are engraved in the throne, one to each side of the world; when it rises they carry it, and it is contained in them until it gathers souls and delights and longings, and comes down full as a tree full of branches and fruit.

As it comes down the four go out engraved and flashing, and sow seed upon the world: עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע. Then the likeness of man goes out, which contains them all — עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי לְמִינוֹ אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ בוֹ. Seed is not brought out but for use: from here, that a man has no leave to bring out seed in vain.

The חָצִיר does not seed, and so does not stand as the others do: it has no likeness to be engraved in at all, but is seen and not seen. Whatever is not figured in form has no standing — it stands for an hour, is eaten by the fire that eats fire, and comes back as before, and so every day.

Man below has form, but does not stand as those above. The forms above are figured as they are, with no other garment, and so stand always; man's form is figured in a garment, and stands for a time and a season. Every night the spirit strips it off and rises, and the consuming fire eats it; afterwards it returns and is figured in its garments. So חֲדָשִׁים לַבְּקָרִים — men are new every day.

Why? רַבָּה אֱמוּנָתֶךָ — great, and not small: great enough to take all the world's children and contain them, upper and lower; a wide place that holds everything and is never filled — כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם וְהַיָּם אֵינֶנּוּ מָלֵא. The sea takes them in and is not filled, and afterwards brings them out as before, and they go.

On this day כִּי טוֹב is written twice, because the day holds both sides and parted the dispute: it said כִּי טוֹב to this side and to that, and made them agree — and so it has וַיֹּאמֶר twice. Here the Name of four letters rises to twelve letters, in four likenesses and four sides, marked upon the holy throne.

יְהִי מְאֹרֹת is written lacking, for croup was created for children. After the first light was hidden away a shell was created for the brain, and that shell spread and brought out another; it rose and fell until it reached the little faces, and sought to cling to them and would not be parted from them. The Holy One parted it and brought it down below, when He created man, to set this right in this world.

When she saw Chavah cleaving to Adam's side and a whole likeness there, she flew, and sought again the little faces; the keepers of the gates would not let her, and the Holy One cast her into the depths of the sea. There she sat until Adam and his wife sinned, and then He brought her out to rule over the children fit to be punished for their fathers' sins. She sat by the flame of the turning sword at the Garden's gate, for she came out of that flame's side.

When that flame turns she wanders the world, finds those children and laughs at them and kills them — all in the diminishing of the moon, and this is מְאֹרֹת. When Cain was born she could not cling to him; afterwards she drew near and bore spirits. Adam served a hundred and thirty years with female spirits until Naamah came, and by her beauty Azza and Azael strayed after her; from her evil spirits and demons spread through the world. Wherever men sleep alone in a house she settles upon them — all in the diminishing of the moon.

מְאֹרֹת — when the moon is set right the letters turn about and it is אִמְרַת יְיָ צְרוּפָה, מָגֵן הוּא לְכֹל הַחֹסִים בּוֹ: a shield against all those evil spirits that wander the world in her diminishing, for all who hold fast to the faith of the Holy One.

When Shlomo went down into the depth of the nut — אֶל גִּנַּת אֱגוֹז יָרַדְתִּי — he took its shell and knew that the delights of those spirits are only to cling to men and defile them: וְתַעֲנוּגֹת בְּנֵי הָאָדָם שִׁדָּה וְשִׁדּוֹת, and the delights men take in the sleep of night bring these out of them. All of it the Holy One had to create, to set the world right by them; and all is brain within and many shells covering it.

From the first point to the end of all the rungs, each is a garment to the next. The first point was an inner light past measuring, until its spreading became a palace to clothe it — itself past measure, yet not so fine as the point within; and that palace spread the first light, which is a garment to it. So each is clothed in the other, this one brain and that one shell, and the shell becomes brain to the rung below — until in this world man is brain and shell, spirit and body, the world's setting right.

While the moon was with the sun in one cleaving she was in light; once parted and appointed over her own hosts she lessened herself and her light, and shells were created upon shells to hide the brain — all of it the brain's own setting right. So יְהִי מְאֹרֹת is written lacking, and all for the setting right of the world: לְהָאִיר עַל הָאָרֶץ.

וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים — at first in one joining, the whole Name together, יְהוָֹ״ה אֱלֹהִים, though by a hidden way. But the moon was not settled beside the sun: she said אֵיכָה תִרְעֶה, and he אֵיכָה תַּרְבִּיץ בַּצָּהֳרָיִם — how shall a small lamp shine at noon? So she lessened herself to be head to those below — צְאִי לָךְ בְּעִקְבֵי הַצֹּאן — and has no light but from the sun. הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל is יְהוָֹ״ה; הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן is אֱלֹהִים, the end of all rungs.

Rungs spread from this side and from that: those from above are מֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם, those from below מֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַלַּיְלָה; וְאֵת הַכּוֹכָבִים are the hosts beyond number, hanging in that רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם, חַי הָעוֹלָמִים. On this day David's kingdom was set right, the fourth leg of the throne; and the fourth day is the day rejected of the builders — אֶבֶן מָאֲסוּ הַבּוֹנִים — because this light lessened itself.

These lights figure the form below, all in the class of Adam: אָדָם אַתֶּם. Every spirit is called Adam, and its body is its garment — עוֹר וּבָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁנִי; wherever it says בְּשַׂר אָדָם, Adam is within and the flesh his garment. So the clean beasts, בְּשַׂר שׁוֹר, the ox within; and so the unclean, בְּשַׂר חֲזִיר. Each kind goes to its kind.

The great light rules by day and the small by night: the male's rule is by day, to bring into his house what it needs; once night comes and the female takes it all, the rule of the house is hers alone — וַתָּקָם בְּעוֹד לַיְלָה וַתִּתֵּן טֶרֶף לְבֵיתָהּ, she and not he. The lights that rise above are מְאוֹרֵי אוֹר, those that go down מְאוֹרֵי אֵשׁ, the rungs that rule the weekdays — and so a blessing is said over the lamp at the going out of Sabbath, when leave is given them to rule.
I:21-22:
Leave is given to look at the fingernails at the going out of Sabbath, for they shine from that lamp to rule. They are the faces without; the fingers within may not be shown to the lamp, for they shine from above and are the inner faces — וְרָאִיתָ אֶת אֲחֹרָי וּפָנַי לֹא יֵרָאוּ. These rule on the Sabbath and those on the weekday.

On the Sabbath the Holy One rules alone by the inner faces upon His throne, bequeathing rest to all the worlds, and the holy people inherit that day. מְאוֹרֵי אוֹר are of the right, the first light of the first day: on the Sabbath they alone shine, and from them all below are lit. When it goes out they are hidden and מְאוֹרֵי הָאֵשׁ rule until Sabbath eve — and so light is taken from the lamp.

וְהַחַיּוֹת רָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב — the eye cannot fix on them. The revealed chayot are those in which the ofan stands, Metatron, greater than the rest by five hundred parasangs. The hidden chayot are beneath the two covered letters י״ה, which rule over ו״ה, these a chariot to those; and the hidden of all hidden, not known at all, rides upon them all.

The upper chayot are contained in רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם, and all hang in it; the firmament above their heads, רָקִיעַ כְּעֵין הַקֶּרַח, is the first. From there onward none can look and know, for it is sealed in thought, and man's thought cannot cleave to it. What hangs upon that thought none can grasp; thought itself, how much more; and within thought, who makes the ideations? There is no understanding to ask, let alone to know.

אֵי״ן סוֹ״ף bears no mark: no question hangs upon it and no idea reaches it. Out of the hidden of the hidden, from the head of the descent of Ein Sof, a fine light shines that is not known, sealed like the point of a needle — the hidden secret of thought, unknown until a light spread from it to the place where the marks of the letters are. From there they come out.

At the head of all, א, head and end of all rungs, the mark in which all are marked, called only אֶחָד: though it holds many likenesses it is one, and upper and lower hang upon it. Its beginning is the concealment of the upper thought, and in its middle six rungs are contained, the hidden upper chayot.

One light shines and is hidden — כְּחֹם הַיּוֹם, when Avraham sat at the opening of the tent, an opening from below upward. The second goes to darken at the turning of evening, the secret of Yitzchak's prayer — וַיֵּצֵא יִצְחָק לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה לִפְנוֹת עָרֶב — and all the darkenings are toward it; in that turning of evening Yaakov was endangered by the prince of Esav.

The third contains the two, a light that shines with healing — וַיִּזְרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, once he was taken into that turning of evening. From then וְהוּא צֹלֵעַ עַל יְרֵכוֹ, which is נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל — יְרֵכוֹ and not יְרֵכָיו, the fourth rung, from which none prophesied until Shmuel: וְגַם נֵצַח יִשְׂרָאֵל, and then it was set right, weak since Yaakov's danger.

וַיִּגַּע בְּכַף יְרֵכוֹ: the prince took strength from that turning of evening in hard judgment. Yaakov was body, contained in two rungs in the secret called Adam, and could not be overcome — וַיַּרְא כִּי לֹא יָכֹל לוֹ — so he took the strength of judgment from outside the body, for the thigh is outside it, and at once וַתֵּקַע כַּף יֶרֶךְ יַעֲקֹב.

Yehoshua prophesied from Moshe's splendour — וְנָתַתָּ מֵהוֹדְךָ עָלָיו — the fifth rung. Netzach is Yaakov's left thigh, and David took it into the right: נְעִימוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶצַח, not יְמִינְךָ but בִּימִינְךָ. Shmuel was afterwards taken into Hod, once he had anointed kings, and is weighed against Moshe and Aharon — מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן בְּכֹהֲנָיו וּשְׁמוּאֵל בְּקֹרְאֵי שְׁמוֹ.

As those three are joined, so Yaakov, Moshe and Yosef. Yaakov was master of the house; when he died Moshe took it; and both served only through Yosef the righteous, for the body does not join the female until it is joined with the covenant — וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ. Yaakov's body was brought whole into the land, for he was the body; of Yosef the bones, which are the hosts above that come out of that righteous one, called צַדִּיק צְבָאוֹת; of Moshe neither, for the Shechinah entered the land, and when he died she returned to her first husband — a woman married to two returns in that world to the first.

Yet Moshe merited in his life what Yaakov did not: Yaakov served her in that world, Moshe in this. When Israel went out of Egypt it was from the side of the Jubilee, and those sixty myriads were of the upper world; not one entered the land, but their children, who are the setting right of the moon. Moshe served the moon while in the body, and when he departed rose in a holy spirit to the upper Jubilee and cleaved to those myriads that were his, where Yaakov returned in spirit into the Shemittah.

וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם. The elder of elders opened: Shimon, Shimon — who said נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם, and what is this אֱלֹהִים here? — and flew away. Hearing himself called Shimon and not Rabbi Shimon, he said: surely this is the Holy One, of whom it is said וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יָתִיב. Now is the hour to open the secret, for leave has been given.

A king had buildings to build, and a craftsman who did nothing but by his leave — וָאֶהְיֶה אֶצְלוֹ אָמוֹן. The king is the supernal Chochmah, the middle pillar the king below; אֱלֹהִים is the craftsman above, the upper Mother, and אֱלֹהִים below, the Shechinah. A wife does nothing without her husband's leave: in Atzilut the Father said, let it be thus, and at once it was — יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר.

Coming to the world of separation, the craftsman said נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ. He said: good to make him, but he will sin before you, being a fool — בֵּן חָכָם יְשַׂמַּח אָב וּבֵן כְּסִיל תּוּגַת אִמּוֹ. She said: since his sin hangs upon the Mother, I will create him in my own likeness — וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם בְּצַלְמוֹ — and the Father did not share in it. When he sinned, וּבְפִשְׁעֵיכֶם שֻׁלְּחָה אִמְּכֶם: He drove him out, and the Mother with him. The wise son is the Adam of Atzilut, the foolish of Beriah.

Is there then a parting between Father and Mother? No: the Adam of Atzilut was male and female from both sides — יְהִי אוֹר from the Father, וַיְהִי אוֹר from the Mother, the two-faced Adam. But this other has neither image nor likeness; the upper Mother had a byname coming to the number of אֱלֹהִים, and that byname is light and darkness — and for the darkness in it the Father said he would sin.

That light is the light created on the first day and hidden for the righteous; that darkness was created on the first day for the wicked — וּרְשָׁעִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ יִדָּמּוּ. So בְּצַלְמֵנוּ is the light and כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ the darkness, a garment to the light as the body is a garment to the soul: עוֹר וּבָשָׂר תַּלְבִּישֵׁנִי.

רְאוּ עַתָּה כִּי אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא וְאֵין אֱלֹהִים עִמָּדִי — the Cause above all causes, from whom every cause takes leave before it acts, as in נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם, where each said to the one above it, let us make. But He has none above and none equal below — וְאֶל מִי תְדַמְּיוּנִי וְאֶשְׁוֶה. There is a one in partnership, male and female, כִּי אֶחָד קְרָאתִיו; He is one without number and without partner.

אֲנִי אָמִית וַאֲחַיֶּה is said in the sefirot: life from the right, death from the left; and if the two do not agree in the middle pillar, judgment does not stand — for they sit as three together.
I:23-24:
Three agree to do judgment, and the Hand comes, stretched out to receive the penitent: the Shechinah is the right hand from Chesed, the left from Gevurah, the hand of יְדוָֹ״ד from the middle pillar. When a man returns, that Hand delivers him. But of the Cause above all causes it is said וְאֵין מִיָּדִי מַצִּיל.

Three times אֲנִי in the verse — three alefs, three yods, three vavs — hinted in the Names. The companions set it against other gods: אֲנִי אֲנִי הוּא is the Holy One and His Shechinah, וְאֵין אֱלֹהִים עִמָּדִי is Samael and the serpent; אֲנִי אָמִית by My Shechinah to the guilty and וַאֲחַיֶּה by her to the innocent.

How many sealed causes are clothed and mounted in the sefirot, the sefirot a chariot to them, hidden from the thought of men — כִּי גָבֹהַּ מֵעַל גָּבֹהַּ שֹׁמֵר. Polished lights one above another, and those that receive are dark before those they receive from; and before the Cause of all causes no light stands at all.

Another word on נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם, which the companions set on the ministering angels: since they knew what was and what was to be, and knew he would sin, why did they want him made? And Azza and Azael accused him — מָה אָדָם וַתֵּדָעֵהוּ: why make him, knowing he will sin before You through his woman, who is darkness? For light is male and darkness female.

The Shechinah said: for this accusation you are to fall — וַיִּרְאוּ בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת בְּנוֹת הָאָדָם — and she cast them from their holiness. Had they not spoken truly? She told them: you came to accuse more than all the host of heaven. He will sin with one woman, you with many — בְּנוֹת and not בַּת; and repentance was made ready for him beforehand.

Why create him at all? Had the good inclination and the evil not been made, which are light and darkness, there would be no merit and no guilt for the Adam of Beriah; he is made of both. Better he were not created, and neither sinned nor earned reward? No: the Torah was created for his sake, and its punishment and reward are only because of him — לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ.

And the Torah of Beriah is a garment for the Shechinah: had man not been created she would be uncovered, like a pauper. So whoever sins is as one stripping her of her garments, and whoever keeps the commandments clothes her — כִּי הִוא כְסוּתֹה לְבַדָּהּ. Darkness is the black of the Torah, light its white.

Yaakov, seeing the pressure of the last exile, וַיִּירָא יַעֲקֹב מְאֹד, divided the holy people in exile into three: the handmaids and their children first, at the head of the exile of Edom, then Leah, then Rachel and Yosef; and seeing their poverty he asked לֶחֶם לֶאֱכֹל וּבֶגֶד לִלְבֹּשׁ.

David said רָעֵב וְעָיֵף וְצָמֵא בַּמִּדְבָּר, for he saw the Shechinah parched and desolate and bore the pain for her; and when he saw Israel return in joy he set ten kinds of song, and last of them all תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי כִי יַעֲטֹף — the prayer that wraps every prayer before it until his own goes in, and so the poor man comes first.

Which is the prayer of the poor? The evening prayer, optional of itself, without her husband — and so she is poor and dry. The seed of Yaakov, righteous and poor, is in the hand of all the nations, like that prayer, which is the night of exile; and the Sabbath prayer is charity to the poor.

So a man must stand as a pauper at the King's gate in the Amidah all six weekdays, for the Shechinah's sake: wrapped in the tzitzit like a poor man and in tefillin like a beggar at the gate that is אֲדֹנָ״י, which comes to the number of הֵיכָ״ל — אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח.

At the evening prayer an eagle comes down on weekdays to take the night's prayer in its wings: Uriel from Chesed, Nuriel from Gevurah, which is burning fire. At Shacharit a lion comes down in its arms and four wings, Michael; at Mincha an ox in its horns, Gavriel. On the Sabbath the Holy One comes down in the three fathers to receive His only daughter — the secret of שַׁבָּת, ש and בַּת — and the upper chayot open and say שְׂאוּ שְׁעָרִים רָאשֵׁיכֶם.

Then seven palaces open: love, fear, mercy, the prophecy of the shining glass, the prophecy of the glass that does not shine, righteousness, judgment. Of them בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא שִׁית, and אֱלֹהִים is the seventh; against them the seven voices of הָבוּ לַיְיָ and its eighteen Names, by which He sails through eighteen worlds. No prayer enters but by measure and by weight.

Prayer is the commandment, which is the Shechinah, and the Torah is the Holy One: no interruption may come between them. All the commandments hang on the Name — שְׁמִי with י״ה, three hundred and sixty-five prohibitions; זִכְרִי with ו״ה, two hundred and forty-eight to do, as many as the words of the Shema, given out of love and fear.

יִשְׂרָאֵל rises in יוּ״ד הֵ״א וָא״ו הֵ״א: Israel rose in thought to be created, for מַחֲשָׁבָה is חָשַׁב מָ״ה. Children, life and sustenance come from the middle pillar, בְּנִי בְכֹרִי יִשְׂרָאֵל, the Tree of Life in which is food for all; and Israel's food to Him is prayer, reckoned as an offering. In exile, הָבָה לִּי בָנִים.

Rising to Him she must take all ten sefirot with her, for there is no sanctity in fewer than ten; and if the serpent would accuse the prayer, a sling must be made against him — זַרְקָא מַקַּף שׁוֹפָר הוֹלֵךְ סְגוֹלְתָּא. Rabbi Shimon opened: upper ones, hear; lower ones, gather. Eliyahu, take leave and come down, for a great battle is ready; Chanoch, come down with all under your hand. Not for my honour, but for the honour of the Shechinah.

As the sling-stone is thrown to a known place, so a man raises his thought in prayer to that crown; whoever straightens, straightens at the Name. While he raises her to her husband, even a serpent wound about his heel he does not interrupt — that stone is the י of Yaakov, אֶבֶן יִשְׂרָאֵל — and he raises her to Ein Sof; bringing her down, whoever bows, bows at בָּרוּךְ.

Sometimes her husband is the ו in the Tzaddik and comes down to her by the six joints of the legs; sometimes he rises to her by the two arms; sometimes he is the son of י״ה, and she is raised to the ה. Rising, she is the crown upon the head of the א, כֶּתֶ״ר, called a tag in the secret of the cantillations; coming down, a point; and when He is united with her she is the seventh of all, the sign of the covenant.

This stone is the builder of all the worlds — אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה וָצֶדֶק יִהְיֶה לָּךְ — the measure between every sefirah, by which each rises to ten: ten cubits between one and the next, a hundred in all. So the stature is measured in the letters of the Name — ו is רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם, its five firmaments one ה and the five heavens of heavens the other — and so the seven earths lie one upon another like the layers of an onion.

י is the small world and ו the long: whoever asks of the long world must lengthen and of the short must shorten. Lengthening in the Name is the tekiah, shortening the shevarim, and between them the teruah of the middle pillar, the shalshelet that holds both. The rising revia answers to the cholam and the shevarim to the sheva: this would raise the voice and that bring it down, and so the shevarim are whispered, the lower Shechinah — וְקוֹלָהּ לֹא יִשָּׁמֵעַ.

אֵלֶּה תוֹלְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ — the initials are תֹּה״וּ, and wherever אֵלֶּה is written it sets aside what came before: these are the generations of tohu, the worlds the Holy One created and destroyed, for which the earth was waste and empty. How create worlds to destroy them? He does not make an end of the work of His hands: He created the world by the Torah, and in that רֵאשִׁית made heaven and earth and supports them by it — for בְּרִית is written within בְּרֵאשִׁית. And she is the land of the living, made of seven earths.
I:25-26:
In tohu there is no foundation, no בְּרִית to support it. The Holy One wished to give the Torah to the nations of the world — and it is circumcision itself — and they would not receive it, and the land was left waste and dry.

יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם אֶל מָקוֹם אֶחָד: the waters are the Torah and the one place is Israel, whose souls hang from the place of בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד יְיָ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ — the glory the lower Shechinah, His place the upper — so the Name rests upon them. The Torah is the settling of the world, and the nations that would not take it were left waste and dry: that is what worlds created and destroyed means, for He makes no end of His own works.

These are the converts. For their sake the small ה of Avraham fell in the fifth thousand, which is ה — waste in the first Temple, dry in the second. Moshe, wishing to bring converts under the wings of the Shechinah, gave them Avraham's letter; and they brought him down, לֶךְ רֵד כִּי שִׁחֵת עַמְּךָ, for they did not receive it in the fear of the י and the love of the ה.

So she fell, and the ו went down with her that she not be lost among them; and having fallen, the ו of Moshe will raise her. He was helped by her and brought her out by the strength of the ו, and then י״ה rested on him and the oath was whole. From generation to generation is Moshe, for no generation is fewer than sixty myriads, and one woman bore sixty myriads at a single birth.

Five kinds are in the mixed multitude — Nefilim, Giborim, Anakim, Refaim, Amalekim — and for their sake the small ה fell from her place. Bilam and Balak were of Amalek: take ע״ם from Bilam and ל״ק from Balak and בָּבֶל remains; and the Amalekim, what was left of the wiping out of all standing things, stand in the fourth exile as heads with great standing, weapons of violence over Israel.

The Nefilim are from the Nefilim above, who accused Adam — מָה אֱנוֹשׁ כִּי תִזְכְּרֶנּוּ — and were told, had you been below as he is you would have sinned more; at once they desired the daughters of men and were cast down in chains, Azza and Azael, from whom the souls of the mixed multitude. The Giborim are men of a name, of the side of נַעֲשֶׂה לָּנוּ שֵׁם, who build synagogues and study halls and set a crowned scroll in them, not for the Name but to make themselves one. The Refaim slacken from Israel in distress, having power to save and not wishing to. The Anakim despise those of whom וַעֲנָקִים לְגַרְגְּרֹתֶיךָ. These returned the world to waste and void, and for them the Temple was destroyed; but the redemption hangs on Amalek, until he is blotted out.

Another word: אֵלֶּה תוֹלְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם are those of whom אֵלֶּה אֱלֹהֶיךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל. On the day these are blotted out it is as though the Holy One made heaven and earth that day, and He will be with His Shechinah and the world made new.

Until then no rain of Torah comes down, and Israel, who are as grasses and trees, do not spring — because וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה. Another word: שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה is the first Mashiach and עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה the second, and they do not come because there is no Moshe there to serve the Shechinah. לֹא יָסוּר שֵׁבֶט מִיהוּדָה is Mashiach ben David, the lawgiver from between his feet Mashiach ben Yosef, and שִׁילֹה is Moshe, the same in number.

Another: שִׂיחַ is ש and חַי, the three branches of the tree that are the three fathers; and עֵשֶׂב is ע״ב and שִׁי״ן, three leaves with seventy-two branches. None is joined in the place that is the Shechinah until he comes who is called אָדָ״ם; the herb does not spring until the Tzaddik springs, and from him אֱמֶת מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח. The scholars, who are the grasses, do not spring in exile until truth springs from the earth — and that is Moshe.

As soon as he comes, וְאֵד יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ: א״ד of אֲדֹנָ״י, with the ו raised in her, becomes אֲדוֹן כָּל הָאָרֶץ, and at once the whole face of the ground is watered — Israel below by the seventy faces of the Torah. Its Targum reads, a cloud shall rise from the earth, the cloud that was upon the Mishkan, and by it the scholars are watered in that hour.

וַיִּיצֶר — these are Israel, whom He forms in the figures of this world and the next, bringing them into His Name: two י with a ו between, which come to the number of יְהוָֹה — the two eyes and the nose, graven as on two precious tablets; and each generation He formed with its upper mate, י״ה, they the ו uniting both. Then He planted them in the holy Garden: וַיִּטַּע is Abba and Imma, גַּן the lower Shechinah, עֵדֶן the upper Mother, אֶת הָאָדָם the middle pillar — she his planting and his mate, never to move from him. In וַיַּצְמַח, the tree pleasant to see is the Tzaddik and the good for food the middle pillar: in exile the Shechinah had food only in the eighteen blessings of prayer, but then he will be food for all.

The Tree of Life will be planted within the Garden, and the tree of the other side — the mixed multitude, the tree of knowing good and evil — will not rule over her, nor will she receive any unclean thing: יְיָ בָּדָד יַנְחֶנּוּ. So converts are not received in the days of Mashiach, and she will be as a vine that takes no graft of another kind. To Israel it was said not to eat of that tree, and on the day they ate they lost two losses, the first Temple and the second — מוֹת תָּמוּת, twice — and caused the river to be waste and dry, the upper Shechinah and the lower, for the flowing of the י to Ein Sof was taken from him.

The moment Israel go out of exile, the holy people alone, that river is וְנָהָר יֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן: the river the middle pillar, עֵדֶן the upper Mother, the garden the lower Shechinah. Then אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל יְיָ, for עֹנֶג is עֵדֶן, נָהָר, גַּן — and אָז יָשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה, not שָׁר but יָשִׁיר. For the mixed multitude עֹנֶג turns to נֶגַע, as the boils broke out on Pharaoh and Egypt; but for Israel it is delight.

And from there it parts into four heads: Chesed the right arm — he who would be wise turns south — watering the camp of Michael with Yehudah and two tribes; Gevurah the left arm — he who would be rich turns north — the camp of Gavriel with Dan and two; Netzach the right leg, Nuriel with Reuven and two; Hod the left leg, of which וְהוּא צֹלֵעַ עַל יְרֵכוֹ, Refael, appointed over the healing of the exile, with Efraim and two.

Another word: the four heads are the four who entered the orchard. One entered by Pishon, פִּי שׁוֹנֶה הֲלָכוֹת; the second by Gichon, where he is buried of whom כָּל הוֹלֵךְ עַל גָּחוֹן; the third by Chidekel, חַד קַל, a sharp swift tongue for expounding; the fourth by Perat, the brain in which is fruitfulness. Ben Zoma and Ben Azzai, who entered among the shells of the Torah, were struck by them; Rabbi Akiva entered the brain, and went in and came out in peace.

Rabbi Akiva said: when you reach the stones of pure marble, do not say water, water, lest you endanger yourselves. They are the stones from which pure waters come, hinted in the א — head and end, with the ו stretched between, which is the Tree of Life; and the two י are hinted in וַיִּיצֶר, two formings, of the upper and of the lower, wisdom at the beginning and wisdom at the end. They answer to the two eyes, from which two tears went down into the great sea: for Moshe was bringing down the Torah of two tablets, and Israel did not merit it, and they broke and fell — and that caused the loss of both Temples. They fell because the ו of וַיִּיצֶר flew from them, and others were given from the side of the tree of knowledge, in permitted and forbidden, life from the right and death from the left.

So do not weigh the stones of pure marble against those other stones, which are life and death — לֵב חָכָם לִימִינוֹ וְלֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ. Those of the tree of knowledge stand in separation; the stones of pure marble stand in union, with no separation at all. And should you say the Tree of Life was taken from them and they fell, so that there is separation — דֹּבֵר שְׁקָרִים לֹא יִכּוֹן לְנֶגֶד עֵינָי, for above there is no separation at all.
I:27-28:
Above, in the Tree of Life, there are no foreign shells — לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע — but the tree below has them, planted in the garden of the small face, which is Chanoch-Metatron: a river goes out of his own delight to water his garden, the orchard where Ben Azzai and Ben Zoma and Elisha entered, and his shells are good on this side and evil on that — forbidden and permitted, clean and unclean. An elder rose and said: so it is, but it is not called the Tree of Life. וַיִּיצֶר, one forming of good and one of evil, is the tree of knowing good and evil, a small Adam, life from one side of him and death from the other.

וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים is the upper Shechinah, Eden, repentance; and the Tree of Life within the garden is the middle pillar, the garden the lower Shechinah. Three knots are bound to him — soul, spirit and breath — and by them וַיְהִי הָאָדָם לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה. Having said this the elder rose and was gone, and Rabbi Shimon said: surely he was an angel.

וַיִּקַּח — from where did He take him? From the four elements of וּמִשָּׁם יִפָּרֵד. So He does with a man, who is made of four elements: when he turns back and labours in the Torah, He parts his soul from their desire and sets him in His own garden, which is the Shechinah — to serve her by the commandments to do and keep her by those not to do. If he merits to keep her he becomes head over the four, a river by which they are watered.

If he transgresses they are watered from the bitterness of the evil tree, and of his limbs it is said וַיְמָרְרוּ אֶת חַיֵּיהֶם — hard labour, the question; בְּחֹמֶר, light to heavy; וּבִלְבֵנִים, the whitening of the law; the field, the Baraita; all their labour, the Mishnah. If they turn back, וַיּוֹרֵהוּ יְיָ עֵץ — the Tree of Life, by which the waters were sweetened, and that is Moshe Mashiach with the staff of God in his hand. The staff is Metatron, life on one side and death on the other: a help while it is a staff, against him when it turns to a serpent. It was given into Moshe's hand as the Oral Torah, and when he struck the rock with it, it was taken back.

וַיְצַו is idolatry, and it sits in the liver — whoever is angry is as one who serves idols. עַל הָאָדָם is bloodshed, and that is the gall, the sword of the angel of death. לֵאמֹר is forbidden union, and that is the spleen, אָכְלָה וּמָחֲתָה פִיהָ, for it has no mouth and is watered from the turbid black blood of the liver. Whoever transgresses these three has his soul exiled in liver, gall and spleen, and is judged in Gehinnom under Mashchit, Af and Chemah.

The forbidden unions are fifteen, the number of י״ה, and six more, the number of ו. Before Israel went into exile with the Shechinah He commanded עֶרְוַת אִמְּךָ לֹא תְגַלֵּה — for the exile is itself the uncovering of the Shechinah's nakedness, וּבְפִשְׁעֵיכֶם שֻׁלְּחָה אִמְּכֶם. That nakedness is Lilith, mother of the mixed multitude, and they are her nakedness.

They stand between the two ה — the upper Shechinah and the lower — so that the ו may not come between them, and while they stand there the Holy One has no leave to draw near: וְנָהָר יֶחֱרַב וְיָבֵשׁ, waste in the upper and dry in the lower, that they be not fed from the ו, which is the Tree of Life. For י is father, ה mother, ו son and ה daughter, and the forbidden unions are said of them. While they are mixed among Israel there is no union in the letters of the Name; the moment they are blotted out, בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד.

So He said אֶעֱשֶׂה לּוֹ עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ: that is the Mishnah, handmaid of the Shechinah — a help to Israel in exile if they merit, from the side of the permitted and clean, and against them if not, from the side of the forbidden and unclean. A woman with blood of purity and blood of niddah is his match but not his mate, for there is no union until the mixed multitude are blotted out; and so Moshe was buried outside the land, and his grave is the Mishnah, and no man knows it to this day.

The beast of the field and the bird of heaven are the unlettered, and even among them no help was found for the Shechinah in exile, nor for Moshe, who never stirred from her. Rabbi Elazar asked who set the story of Adam upon Israel and upon Moshe, and was answered: have you not learned מַגִּיד מֵרֵאשִׁית אַחֲרִית? So Moshe did not die, and he is called Adam; and of him it is said in the last exile וּלְאָדָם לֹא מָצָא עֵזֶר — all of them against him.

Then וַיַּפֵּל יְיָ אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם: Abba and Imma, and the deep sleep is exile, for sleep is nothing else. From the maidens of the Matrona they took one, the white side, fair as the moon; and the flesh beneath her is the flesh of Moshe, which is red — פְּנֵי מֹשֶׁה כִּפְנֵי חַמָּה. The rib is of Chesed, which is white, the flesh of Gevurah, which is red, and she is held in both: שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי.

וַיִּבֶן אֶת הַצֵּלָע hints the secret of levirate marriage, that once he has not built he shall not build again; but of the Holy One it is said that He builds — בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְיָ — Abba and Imma building her for the ו, who is their son. Of her it is said וַאֲנִי אֶהְיֶה לָּהּ חוֹמַת אֵשׁ סָבִיב, and so the Temple on that mountain will be built by His own hand and stand for all generations: the first was built by the hand of man and this by His.

זֹאת הַפַּעַם עֶצֶם מֵעֲצָמַי is the Shechinah, the betrothed maiden, said to the middle pillar; לְזֹאת יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה from the upper side, which is the Mother, and כִּי מֵאִישׁ לֻקֳחָה from the side of Abba. In that hour every one of Israel will attain his mate — וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב חָדָשׁ — for these are the new souls, and the son of David does not come until all the souls in the body are spent. Then the mixed multitude pass from the world, and nakedness passes with them.

וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם — cunning for evil beyond all the beasts of the nations. They are the children of the primeval serpent that seduced Chavah, and the mixed multitude are the very filth he cast into her; from that filth came Cain, who killed Hevel — בְּשַׁגַּם הוּא בָשָׂר, and בְּשַׁגַּ״ם is מֹשֶׁ״ה. Yet Moshe, to cover his father's nakedness, took the daughter of Yitro, called Keini because he parted from Cain, and afterwards wished to bring the mixed multitude back in repentance — for the Holy One joins a good thought to the deed, though He warned him they were of an evil stock.

For their sake Israel were driven out — וַיְגָרֶשׁ אֶת הָאָדָם, and Adam is Israel; and for their sake Moshe was kept from the land, for through them he sinned at the rock, when he had been told only to speak to it. Of them He said מִי אֲשֶׁר חָטָא לִי אֶמְחֶנּוּ מִסִּפְרִי, for they are of the seed of Amalek and caused the two tablets to be broken. Then Israel knew they were naked under the burden of Egypt, being without Torah; and what is מֹשֶׁ״ה turns for the mixed multitude to שַׁמָּ״ה, hinting that he will return among them in the last exile.

When the tablets were broken, וַיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה: they covered themselves in many shells from the mixed multitude, that their nakedness be not uncovered, and their covering is the corners of the tzitzit and the straps of the tefillin; and וַיַּעֲשׂוּ לָהֶם חֲגֹרֹת is חֲגוֹר חַרְבְּךָ עַל יָרֵךְ גִּבּוֹר, the reading of Shema. They heard the voice when they drew near to Sinai, and there the mixed multitude died: they were the ones who said וְאַל יְדַבֵּר עִמָּנוּ אֱלֹהִים and let the Torah go — the unlettered, of the side of that serpent of whom אָרוּר אַתָּה מִכָּל הַבְּהֵמָה.
I:29-32:
The wicked are the world's harmers in fact, and demons and spirits and liliot are mingled among Israel; but none is cursed like Amalek, the evil serpent, a strange god — uncovered to every nakedness, a murderer, his mate the poison of death. All of it is Samael, and there is Samael and Samael, not all alike; that side of the serpent is cursed above them all. אַיֶּכָּה hinted to Adam that the Temple would be destroyed and wept over with אֵיכָה — אַ״י כֹּ״ה — and in time to come every evil kind will be cleared from the world and all return to its place: בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא יִהְיֶה יְיָ אֶחָד וּשְׁמוֹ אֶחָד.

Every שְׁלֹמֹה in the Song of Songs is the King whose peace is His; plain מֶלֶךְ is the female, and the lower inherits from the upper and the two are one — the בַּיִת of בְּחָכְמָה יִבָּנֶה בָּיִת. Before He created the world His Name was sealed within Him, and nothing stood until He wrapped Himself in one wrapping of splendour and created it, bringing out great cedars from that light and setting His chariot on the twenty-two letters graven in the ten utterances: אַפִּרְיוֹן עָשָׂה לוֹ הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה מֵעֲצֵי הַלְּבָנוֹן, אַרְזֵי לְבָנוֹן אֲשֶׁר נָטָע. And לוֹ — for Himself, for His own setting right, to show the supernal glory and make known that He is one and His Name one.

The upper river goes down and makes of it the great sea: כָּל הַנְּחָלִים הֹלְכִים אֶל הַיָּם וְהַיָּם אֵינֶנּוּ מָלֵא, for it gathers all and draws it in — and שָׁרוֹן is nothing but the place of that great sea which draws in all the waters of the world: one brings out and one draws in, and they light one another by known ways. So the upper house is the settling of the world and plain מֶלֶךְ the house below; and וְהַמֶּלֶךְ יִשְׂמַח בֵּאלֹהִים is the lower world rejoicing in the upper, in the light that goes out by one hidden path and enters it, the two being one. These are called the life of the King, and that is the root of the house.

The house builds the house of the world: בְּרֵאשִׁית is ב and רֵאשִׁית, and רֵאשִׁית is Chochmah when it gathers all into itself and becomes a great sea — a sea whose waters have congealed, מִבֶּטֶן מִי יָצָא הַקָּרַח, frozen so as to draw in others. That ice does not let its waters flow except when the strength of the south reaches it: then what froze on the north side is loosed and flows to water all the beasts of the field, יַשְׁקוּ כָּל חַיְתוֹ שָׂדָי, which are called the mountains of separation.

When thought rose in desire from the hidden of all hidden, one river was drawn out of it; and where they draw near by a path known neither above nor below is the beginning of all. בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם — it brought out a voice, the voice of the shofar; the heavens rule over the earth by the life of the upper King, and the earth is fed from it — וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ, with the וא״ו added to rule over her food. אֵ״ת is the force holding the twenty-two letters, א to ת, which this אֱלֹהִים gave to the heavens, and וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ is the joining of male and female graven in them. The upper אֱלֹהִים made heaven and earth by the force of the beginning of all, and the same secret comes down, where the last one makes a heaven and an earth below: so the ב is two worlds, each after the pattern of the other, and each brings out two.

The upper goes down into the lower and is filled by one rung that rests on it, as by that sealed path above — except that the one below is an אֹרַח, וְאֹרַח צַדִּיקִים כְּאוֹר נֹגַהּ, and the one above a fine נָתִיב, נָתִיב לֹא יְדָעוֹ עָיִט: הַנּוֹתֵן בַּיָּם דֶּרֶךְ וּבְמַיִם עַזִּים נְתִיבָה. The upper world, filled and made pregnant as a female from a male, brings out two children as one, male and female, and they are heaven and earth. The earth is fed from the waters of heaven, and the lower waters call to the upper as a female open to a male, casting her waters against his to make seed.

שְׂאוּ מָרוֹם עֵינֵיכֶם וּרְאוּ מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה. The letters were graven in the work of all and then marked in the verse: ב in בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא, female, and א in אֱלֹהִים אֵת, male; ה brought out heaven to give it life, and ו brought out the earth to give it food, taking אֵ״ת, the whole twenty-two, so that the earth gathers them all into herself. And when the blazing fire is roused from the left it takes hold and the smoke rises — וְהַר סִינַי עָשַׁן כֻּלּוֹ — so that all stands on the left side: אַף יָדִי יָסְדָה אֶרֶץ וִימִינִי טִפְּחָה שָׁמָיִם, the male from the right and the female from the left.

Thus far the words are taken up beyond asking, for Chochmah is perfected out of אַיִן and does not stand to be asked, being sealed and deep. Once the deep light spread, its light stands to be asked, and it is called by the mouth of the question, מִ״י — מִי בָרָא אֵלֶּה. One may not ask what is above or below, only the place from which they come out — and even then to stand at the question and not to know it. Is רֵאשִׁית an utterance? Before its force spread, all was sealed within it and it is בְּרֵאשִׁית and an utterance together; once the forces went out it is called רֵאשִׁית and is an utterance alone. מִ״י is the question, the one who created אֵלֶּה; and when it spread and was perfected it became יָ״ם and created below, everything after the pattern above. עַד שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ בִּמְסִבּוֹ is the settling in the lower kingdom, by the path sealed and not known; and נִרְדִּי נָתַן רֵיחוֹ is the lower king, who created the world below after the pattern above.

In two colours the world was created, right and left, in six upper days — כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה יְיָ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ — and these dug ways and made the sixty holes to the great deep, so the שִׁיתִין were created from the six days of the beginning and were the peace of the world. וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ is what was at first and did not stand — הָיְתָה, already, and afterwards it stood. In forty-two letters the world was graven, all of them the crowning of the holy Name: joined, they rise above and come down below and are crowned in the four sides of the world, and the world can stand.

They struck at the scales of the great serpent and went in beneath the holes of the dust a thousand five hundred cubits; then the great deep rose in darkness and darkness covered all, until the light came out and split it — מְגַלֶּה עֲמֻקוֹת מִנִּי חֹשֶׁךְ. The waters were weighed in a scale, three drops within it, half for standing and half going down, these rising and those descending; and when they rose by the lifting of the hand the scale stood straight, turning neither right nor left: מִי מָדַד בְּשָׁעֳלוֹ מַיִם.

All was in the earth, sealed and unrevealed — strength and force, and waters frozen within her that neither flowed nor spread — until the light from above shone on her and struck her shell and her strength was loosed: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר, the first supernal light that was from before. From here all the forces came out, and the earth was sweetened and brought out her hosts. When it shone, its light rose from the world's end to the world's end; when He looked at the wicked it was hidden away, and it goes out only by sealed paths.

וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב. Every dream that stands in כִּי טוֹב is peace above and below, and one who sees ט — good for him and for his dream, for the Torah opened with it and it shines from the world's end to the world's end. ט is the ninth of all, lit from the upper beginning and taken into it, made in the sealing of the point that is the secret of י; ו comes out of its force, and by it the heavens were made; and when it is sealed in one point and stored within, ב shines, and from it upper and lower come out — the upper hidden, the lower revealed. These three letters טוֹ״ב were afterwards taken into the Righteous of the world, who holds all above and below: אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב.

בְּרֵאשִׁית is the secret of רֵאשִׁית עֲרִסֹתֵיכֶם חַלָּה תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה, the upper Chochmah; and ב is the house of the world, watered from that river which enters it — וְנָהָר יֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן, gathering all from the upper depth, its waters never ceasing. That depth is the first house, and in it the letters are sealed by one fine path stored within; and from it two forces came out — אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם, not שָׁמַיִם but הַשָּׁמַיִם, and וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ, which the sealed one brought out though she was within the class of heaven. They came out together, cleaving side to side, and when the beginning of all shone the heavens took her and set her in her place.

When the earth returned to her place and was parted from the sides of heaven she was waste and void, longing to cleave to them as at first, because she saw the heavens shining and herself darkened — until the upper light went out upon her and lit her, and she came back to look at the heavens face to face, and the earth was set right and sweetened. The light came out on the right and the darkness on the left, and He parted them so that each be taken into the other. Not a true separation: day comes from the side of light, which is the right, and night from the side of darkness, which is the left, and the parting was from their own sides, that they look face to face and cleave and all be one.

He is called day and she night — וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה, the darkness that holds to night, which has no light of its own; and though she came from the side of fire, which is darkness, darkness is not lit until it is lit from the side of day. Day lights the night, and night does not shine until the time of וְלַיְלָה כַּיּוֹם יָאִיר כַּחֲשֵׁיכָה כָּאוֹרָה.

Rabbi Elazar opened: קוֹל יְיָ עַל הַמָּיִם — the upper voice appointed over the waters that flow from rung to rung until they gather to one place, sending each on its own way as a gardener sends water where it is due. אֵל הַכָּבוֹד הִרְעִים is the side that comes from Gevurah, or the right from which the left goes out; and עַל מַיִם רַבִּים is the upper Chochmah, over that sealed depth which comes out of it: וּשְׁבִילְךָ בְּמַיִם רַבִּים.

Rabbi Shimon opened: לְעֻמַּת הַמִּסְגֶּרֶת תִּהְיֶיןָ הַטַּבָּעֹת בָּתִּים לְבַדִּים. The מִסְגֶּרֶת is a closed place, open only by one fine path known in hiding to it, by which it is filled and marks out gates for the kindling of lamps; being sealed it is called so, and it is the World to Come. The rings are the supernal circles held one in another — water from spirit, spirit from fire, fire from water — all looking toward it, where the upper river is joined to water them. They are houses and places for the staves, the chariots below, one from the side of fire, one of water, one of spirit, all to be a chariot for the Ark; so whoever draws near, let him draw near by the staves and not by what is within — go round about, they say to the Nazirite, and do not come near the vineyard — except those fit to serve within: וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת.

The בֵּי״ת of בְּרֵאשִׁית is great. What are the six days of the beginning? אַרְזֵי לְבָנוֹן אֲשֶׁר נָטָע — as those cedars come out of Lebanon, so the six days come out of בְּרֵאשִׁית, and the verse sets them out: לְךָ יְיָ הַגְּדֻלָּה וְהַגְּבוּרָה וְהַתִּפְאֶרֶת, where כִּי כֹל is the Righteous, the heaven is Tiferet and the earth Knesset Yisrael — the foundation of the world, called כֹּל, holding them both. She is second in the count and yet is called the beginning, because the upper crown, hidden away, is first and does not enter the count; and as the upper Chochmah is רֵאשִׁית, so is the lower, and the ב is not to be parted from it. בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים is that river going out of Eden to water the garden and look to all it needs, for אֱלֹהִים is אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים and the creating is by its hand; and when all had settled in its place as one, that last circle itself became רֵאשִׁית, and in it He brought out upper lights and set the waters flowing to be received below.

Rabbi Yehuda said: הֲיִתְפָּאֵר הַגַּרְזֶן עַל הַחֹצֵב בּוֹ — whose is the praise, is it not the craftsman's? So in this beginning the upper אֱלֹהִים created the heavens, and the praise is His. Rabbi Yosi said of אֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֱלֹהִים קְרֹבִים אֵלָיו that it should have said קָרוֹב: but they are the upper אֱלֹהִים, the אֱלֹהִים of the fear of Yitzchak, and the last — many Gevurot coming out of one, and all of them one. A Tosefta: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא hints at Keter and Chochmah, אֱלֹהִים at Binah, אֵת at Gedulah and Gevurah, הַשָּׁמַיִם is Tiferet, וְאֵת hints at Netzach, Hod and Yesod, and הָאָרֶץ at Malchut.

יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי אוֹר is the light the Holy One created first, the light of the eye, which He showed the first man, who saw by it from the world's end to the world's end; the light He showed David, and the light He showed Moshe, who saw by it from Gilad to Dan. Seeing that three wicked generations would arise — Enosh, the Flood, the Dispersion — He hid it away, and gave it to Moshe, who used it the three months left him of his months of carrying: וַתִּצְפְּנֵהוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה יְרָחִים. When he came before Pharaoh it was taken from him, until he stood on Sinai and it was given back; he used it all his days, and Israel could not come near him until he set a veil on his face, for he wrapped himself in it as in a tallit — עֹטֶה אוֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָה.

It was hidden that the wicked should not have joy of it and the worlds not be enjoyed for their sake, and it is stored for the righteous — for the Righteous exactly: אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק וּלְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה. Then the worlds will be sweetened and all be one; and until the World to Come arrives it is hidden and sealed. That light came out from within the darkness graven in the shells of the hidden of all, until from it a path was graven to the darkness below and the light rested in it — and the darkness below is what is called night.

מְגַלֶּה עֲמֻקוֹת מִנִּי חֹשֶׁךְ: the sealed supernal crowns are revealed only out of that darkness which is the secret of night. All the deep sealed things that come out of thought and are carried by the voice are not revealed until speech reveals them — and speech is דִּבּוּר, which is called Shabbat. Because Shabbat is called speech, weekday speech is forbidden on it: this speech must rule and no other.
