And this speech, coming from the side of darkness, reveals depths from within itself — מִנִּי חֹשֶׁךְ, exactly.

Then what of וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ? Light brought out day and darkness brought out night, and afterwards He joined them and they were one — וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד, for night and day are called one; and that parting is said of the time of exile, where division is found. Thus far the male is in light and the female in darkness, and afterwards they join to be one. How are they parted? The rungs are parted and the two are one, for there is no light but in darkness and no darkness but in light; though they are parted in their colours, they are one — יוֹם אֶחָד.

Rabbi Shimon said: upon the covenant the world was created and stands — אִם לֹא בְרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלָיְלָה חֻקּוֹת שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ לֹא שָׂמְתִּי. And the covenant is the Righteous, foundation of the world, the secret of זָכוֹר; so the world stands by the covenant, day and night as one, and the statutes of heaven flow out of the upper Eden. מִקּוֹל מְחַצְצִים בֵּין מַשְׁאַבִּים is the voice of Yaakov, the man between, sitting between those who draw water from above, taking from two sides and holding them within himself; there is the place of faith to cleave to, and there they suckle and draw. צִדְקוֹת פִּרְזוֹנוֹ is the Righteous of the world, who draws all and scatters the upper waters to the great sea — in Israel, for Israel inherited this covenant as an inheritance of worlds.

Once Israel forsook it, circumcising and not uncovering, אָז יָרְדוּ לַשְּׁעָרִים עַם יְיָ — they sat at the gates of righteousness and did not enter — until Devorah came and moved them to it: בִּפְרֹעַ פְּרָעוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל. So חָדְלוּ פְרָזוֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל is that same covenant left uncovered; and שַׁקַּמְתִּי אֵם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — what is אֵם? I brought the upper waters down to sustain the worlds, to show that the world stands on nothing but this covenant: וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם.

Three come out of one; one stands in three; it enters between two; two suckle one; one suckles many sides — and then all is one: וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד, a day holding evening and morning together, the secret of the covenant of day and night. A Tosefta: one who circumcises and does not uncover is as one who has not circumcised, for they are two rungs — milah and priah, זָכוֹר and שָׁמוֹר, צַדִּיק and צֶדֶק, male and female; the sign of the covenant is Yosef and the covenant is Rachel, and they must be joined, and he has made a parting between them.

יְהִי רָקִיעַ בְּתוֹךְ הַמָּיִם. Seven firmaments are above, all standing in supernal holiness; this one is in the midst of the waters, above the other chayot, parting the upper waters from the lower — the lower call to the upper and drink from it, for all the waters are held in it, and afterwards it brings them down to those chayot. גַּן נָעוּל אֲחֹתִי כַלָּה, גַּל נָעוּל — a garden locked, for all is sealed and held in it; a spring locked, for that river flows and enters and is held and does not go out, and the waters congeal and stand, because the north wind blows on them and they freeze until ice is made. Were it not for the side of the south, which strikes the strength of that ice, its waters would never come out; and the look of that upper firmament is as the look of that ice.

And is the firmament in the middle of the waters? יְהִי is written: what comes out of it is in the midst of the waters, and it itself stands above, on the head of the chayot. There is a membrane in the middle of a man's bowels which divides from below upward, drawing from above and giving below; and just so this firmament stands in the middle, over the chayot below, parting the upper waters from the lower. Those waters were taken away and bore darkness, and on this secret it is written וְהִבְדִּילָה הַפָּרֹכֶת לָכֶם בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים.

Rabbi Abba opened: הַמְקָרֶה בַמַּיִם עֲלִיּוֹתָיו — the upper waters of all, with which the house was made ready: בְּחָכְמָה יִבָּנֶה בָּיִת וּבִתְבוּנָה יִתְכּוֹנָן. In הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ, Rabbi Yeisa the elder divided עָבִים into ע״ב and יָ״ם: the cloud that is darkness, the left, standing over that sea; and הַמְהַלֵּךְ עַל כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ is the spirit of the upper sanctuary — וַיִּרְכַּב עַל כְּרוּב וַיָּעֹף וַיֵּדֶא עַל כַּנְפֵי רוּחַ: He rode upon one keruv and was afterwards revealed on the wings of the spirit, and until this was roused He was not revealed in that.

וּמַיִם תִּכֵּן בְּמִדָּה — by measure exactly He set them when they reached her, and they are the setting right of the world when they come from the side of Gevurah. So the ancients would say: when they reached this place the lips of the wise moved and they said nothing at all, that they should not be punished.
I:3-4:
The letters go on presenting themselves. Samech is told to stay where she is: the fallen lean on her, סוֹמֵךְ יְיָ לְכָל הַנּוֹפְלִים, and if she leaves her place what becomes of them? Mem is King, and is sent back for that very reason — the world may not stand without a king. Kaf comes down from under the Throne of Glory and two hundred thousand worlds shake with her, and she is sent back to her throne, since כָּלָה is heard in her. Yod is the beginning of the holy Name and cannot be taken out of it. Tet’s goodness is hidden inside her. Zayin has the sword. Dalet and Gimel are told to stay together and not to part: Dalet is the poor one, Gimel deals kindly with her, and the poor will not cease from the world.

Bet says: in me they bless You above and below — and with her the world is made. Alef alone does not come in. Asked why, she says she saw all the letters leave with nothing, and besides, the King has given Bet a great gift and it is not fitting to take back what was given to one and hand it to another. She is answered: though the world is created with Bet, you shall be the head of all the letters; there is no oneness in Me except in you. So the upper letters were made great and the lower small, and the verse carries both — בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא with Bet, אֱלֹהִים אֵת with Alef.

R. Yudai reads בְּרֵאשִׁית as בְּחָכְמָה, and the folio turns to the key. Everything was engraved and hidden away as a man hides all he has under one key, and the key put in one palace; and in that palace are fifty gates, forty-nine engraved to the four sides and one that has no side at all, so that none knows whether it is above or below. In those gates is a lock, and one narrow place to put the key in, marked by nothing but the key’s own mark. בְּרֵאשִׁית is that key: it holds all and shuts and opens. While the matter stayed shut in the word בָּרָא the world was not and did not stand, and tohu covered everything. When did the key open the gates? When Abraham came.

Then the folio breaks off into grief. R. Chiya throws himself down and kisses the dust and weeps: dust, dust, how stubborn you are, how insolent — everything the eye desires wears out in you, you eat and grind down every pillar of light in the world; and the holy lamp that lit the world is given to you. He fasts forty days to be shown R. Shimon and is told he is not permitted; fasts forty more, and is shown R. Shimon and R. Eleazar his son rising on great wings to the academy of the firmament, renewed and brighter than the light of the sun. R. Shimon says: let R. Chiya come in and see how the Holy One is going to renew the faces of the righteous in the time to come. Happy is he who comes in here without shame.
I:33-34:
Waters and letters settle one into another until a building stands on them; upper waters mingle with lower and bring out the house of the world, which is why ב stands at the head. They rose and fell until the firmament divided them, and the second day is a day of division, for Gehinnom was made in it. R. Yehuda takes his rule from here: a dispute for the sake of Heaven endures, and this one did — the heavens were established by it, as the parochet divides precisely in the middle.

They gather to the place called One, the lower sea that completes the One — R. Yeisa’s place of וּבְרִית שְׁלוֹמִי לֹא תָמוּט, which takes all and casts it into the sea, and by which the earth is set in order. Why dry land? R. Yitzchak reads לֶחֶם עֹנִי as poor bread: she drinks every water of the world and is dry still, until that place fills her.

The gathering itself R. Chiya calls the Tzadik — אִמְרוּ צַדִּיק כִּי טוֹב — seas in the plural, because every stream runs into him; R. Yosei calls it Israel, מִקְוֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל יְיָ. Being inscribed he divides the first day from the third, and between them כִּי טוֹב is not said, for it was on the third that the earth bore fruit by his power: the tree that makes fruits is the tree of knowing good and evil, the one who makes fruit the Tzadik, foundation of the world.

לְמִינוֹ is the mark of that kind, the holy covenant, inscribed in whoever bears a holy spirit, and the children of faith are never parted from it. The mark is given on the eighth day that a child resemble his mother, the eighth grade, before whom the soul that flew from her must appear at eight days; the priah uncovers it that he resemble his father — the tree that makes fruit the mother, the maker of fruit the father. אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ בוֹ is the seed of the וא"ו in it, cast on the earth: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, for from these they came and these they resemble.

עֹשֶׂה אֶרֶץ בְּכֹחוֹ is read for its tense: not made but makes, continually; His power is the Tzadik, His wisdom Tzedek. R. Yehuda brings from R. Elazar’s engraved letters the knots of twenty-two bound as one, where of two the risen descends and the descended rises; R. Yosei sets the balance-beam in the middle, the tongue that weighs, whose secret is the holy shekel — which R. Yehuda calls the Holy Spirit. The lower heavens were made by the word of the upper, the spirit carrying the voice to that river whose waters never cease.

יְהִי מְאֹרֹת is written defective, and the force of judgment rests in it. Below it is the moon, on whom hang the croup that takes children and the curse itself, she being the smallest of the lights and darkening at times to receive none; she hangs on the firmament that gathers every light and lights what does not shine, and the other forces hang from her because her light is small. Without its vav the word is death in the world, and on it everything hangs, to take Lilith in. R. Elazar: she is the mirror that does not shine of itself, a lantern gathering light. The Ark is that mirror, a chest for the Written Torah; the covenant is the sun that lights her, and from him she takes her name — as Tzadik and Tzedek, so Adon and Adonai hang one on the other.

Stars and constellations are engraved in that firmament and hang from it to give light, the moon there and the sun with her, and on them hang the appointed times and festivals, the months and Sabbaths. Seven stars stand against seven firmaments and govern the world, the upper world above them; two worlds, the lower patterned on the upper, a king above and a king below. יְיָ מֶלֶךְ, יְיָ מָלָךְ, יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ R. Acha reads downward — the World to Come, Tiferet Yisrael, the Ark of the Covenant — and David turned them upward, the King below and וָעֶד above, where the completeness of all is.

R. Abba: the firmament that lights the earth is the river that flows out of Eden. When the moon rules and is lit from it the hosts below gain light, the stars over the earth make plants and trees grow, even the fish of the sea increase, and many officers of judgment roam abroad — for when there is joy in the king’s house even those of the gatehouses rejoice, and the children of the world must be guarded. Then she lessens her light before the sun, all she takes being so that he may shine through her: a lessening undone only in the seven days of the millu’im, when the world is sweetened and the serpent does not diminish her, in the time of בִּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח.

The lower waters swarm with forces patterned on those above, and the upper brought out the soul of the first Adam. The birds over the earth are messengers seen in a man’s shape; others are seen only as spirit, as a man can understand them. Leviathan and his mate are the great creatures, the creeping soul Lilith. The six-winged birds never change their kind: they roam the world, see men’s deeds and carry them up — גַּם בְּמַדָּעֲךָ מֶלֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּל. R. Chizkiyah reads the creeping as the night creeping in, when they rule and open in song at the three watches and are not silent.

R. Shimon rose: when the Holy One wished to make Adam, all above and below trembled, and the sixth day climbed its grades until the supernal will lit the beginning of all lights. The east opened; the south strengthened the east, the east the north; the north called the west to join it, the south took hold of the west, and south and north went round it as the fences of a garden — and the west, asking of them all, said נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ, that he be of this pattern, four directions and above and below. East cleaved to west and brought him out: Adam came from the place of the Temple. His name is the secret of the letters: א one above, the closed ם of לְםַרְבֵּה הַמִּשְׂרָה, the ד hidden in the west. Male and female came down together; she clung to his side until He cast a sleep on him, and he lay in the place of the Temple below, and the Holy One sawed him apart and arrayed her as a bride. In the books of the ancients this is Lilith the first, who conceived from him and was no help corresponding to him. Adam was last of all, as was fitting — that he come into a world already complete. And R. Shimon opens on the plants of the field…
I:35-36:
The plants of the field are the great trees, waiting to be planted. Adam and Eve were made side by side and not face to face, because it had not yet rained and the union was not in its order; set right below, so it was found above. The Mishkan proves it — until it was raised below it was not raised above — and so does the samech missing from the portion until here, for the samech is עֵזֶר, the help that turns them face to face. When Eve was completed Adam was completed, and not before.

Then the mist that rises from the earth, the repair below, which is the longing of the female toward the male, and only after it the watering: smoke rises first and the cloud wakes, as the smoke of the offering makes completion above. Were Knesset Yisrael not to begin the waking, nothing above would wake toward her.

R. Abba on the two trees: the Tree of Life is a journey of five hundred years, at the middle of the garden, and all the waters of Creation divide beneath it — the river rests on the garden and enters it, and from her they go out in streams that water the upper mountains of pure balsam. The other does not stand at the middle, and is called of good and evil because it sucks from two sides and knows them, as one who sucks sweet and bitter. Held in it are the cedars of Lebanon, the six upper days.

The support is the closing of flesh beneath her: she was at his side, and the Holy One uprooted them and planted them elsewhere, face to face, to endure — so the worlds are propped. That they were plantings R. Abba takes from נֵצֶר מַטָּעַי מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי, no other creature having laboured in them, and from בְּיוֹם נִטְעֵךְ תְּשַׂגְשֵׂגִי, for on the day they were planted they sinned. They were like the horns of locusts, their light thin, and once planted grew in light; Adam and Eve gave off no scent until they were uprooted, replanted and set right.

Seven commands are read word by word out of וַיְצַו יְיָ אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָדָם לֵאמֹר — idolatry, blessing the Name, the judges, bloodshed, forbidden union, then theft and a limb from the living. All the trees were permitted him, to eat in unity, for the Patriarchs and all the prophets ate and lived; but this one is the tree of death, and whoever takes it alone takes the poison of death, for he parts the plantings. R. Yehuda asked what it means that Adam drew his foreskin; R. Shimon: he parted the covenant from its place and clung to the foreskin, enticed by the serpent. The fruit of the tree is the woman, whose feet go down to death — the garden the river entered and watered while all was one, for from there downward is parting.

Of the serpent R. Yitzchak says the evil inclination and R. Yehuda an actual serpent; R. Shimon rules all is one — Samael, who came down from heaven riding it, whose shape all creatures saw and fled. With wisdom he brought curses on the world and ruined the first tree, and the matter hung on him until Jacob came, whose beauty was Adam’s, and took the blessings back, that Samael not be blessed above nor Esau below — וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ. He is the angel of death, and so brought death to all the world: קֵץ כָּל בָּשָׂר, who takes the soul from all flesh.

He opened with אַף, with anger, and cast anger into the world, telling her that with this tree God made the world and that eating of it they would be as God. R. Yehuda corrects him word by word: to say God made the world with it would have been proper, an axe in the hand of the hewer — what he said was that God ate of it and then made the world, and every craftsman hates his fellow, so eat and be makers of worlds. R. Yitzchak: they spoke falsehood throughout, the first word already false, for all the trees were permitted. And all those commands hang on this tree — idolatry in the great appointed ones, bloodshed in the tree itself, on the side of Gevurah, over which Samael is set, and forbidden union, for she is a woman, and none may be alone with a woman save with her husband — so eating of it he transgressed them all. He added of his own: I touched it and did not die; put your hand to it and you will not die.

With what did she see? R. Yitzchak: the tree gave off scent, and for it she desired to eat; R. Yosei: it was sight, by the measure of the tree she took, the opening of their eyes coming only after. She saw and did not see, and took of its fruit and not of it, clinging to the place of death and bringing death on all the world. By that sin came the parting of a woman from her husband, which is the parting of voice from speech, and whoever parts them is struck dumb and given to the dust. R. Shimon: נֶאֱלַמְתִּי דוּמִיָּה is Knesset Yisrael in exile, the voice parted from her so the word is not heard; and לְךָ דֻמִיָּה תְהִלָּה — for Your sake she is silent.

She pressed grapes and gave him, for in this tree death rests and it rules at night; when she rules the whole world tastes the taste of death — save the children of faith, who give their souls into His keeping, and a deposit returns to its place: וֶאֱמוּנָתְךָ בַּלֵּילוֹת. R. Chiya: their eyes were opened to know the evils of the world, and knowing evil they knew they were naked, having lost the radiance that covered them. They sewed the leaves of that tree to cover themselves in its images and, seeing that this world is conducted by those leaves, made weapons of them, knowing then all the sorcery of the world.

R. Yehuda: three entered into judgment, and the lower world was cursed by the filth of the serpent and did not stand until Israel stood at Sinai. Then garments of light were exchanged for garments of skin — the light the upper angels had come to take pleasure in, and now a skin in which the skin takes pleasure and not the soul. Two came upon Eve and she bore two, each to his kind: from Cain’s side the evil weapons and the spirits and demons and sorcerers; from Abel’s a side of more mercy but not complete, good wine in bad, unset right until Seth, from whom the righteous generations are traced and by whom the world was planted — while from Cain come all the insolent and the guilty.

R. Elazar: Cain was afraid, seeing armed camps coming to kill him, and turning in repentance said וּמִפָּנֶיךָ אֶסָּתֵר — I shall be hidden from my own building, hidden from those faces that they not watch over him, and so every one who finds him will kill him. The sign set on him is one letter of the twenty-two, for his protection. R. Yehuda: the field is the woman, and from that side he inherited killing, from Samael who brought death to all the world, and he was jealous of Abel over her; R. Chiya holds it was his offering unaccepted, and is answered that all of it was of a piece. אִם תֵּיטִיב שְׂאֵת — the firstborn has praise in everything, and it hangs on his deeds. And what is the opening at which sin crouches…
I:37-38:
The opening is the upper one from which judgments go out on the world’s deeds, and crouching at it is the angel of death. Adam was born on Rosh Hashana, the day barren women are remembered, and coming out on that day he came out in judgment; the world has stood in judgment since. וְאַתָּה תִּמְשָׁל בּוֹ is read with וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם: the Holy One does not rule until the wicked are spent, and once the destroyer has made an end of them He rules over him, that he not harm the world — and R. Yehuda, that a man rules him by repentance.

Cain’s generations went about battering the earth, resembling those above and below. Samael had cast filth into Eve and she bore Cain, whose face was unlike other men’s, and his line were called only בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים; Azza and Azael, fallen from their holy place, saw the daughters of men and bore the Nefilim. Sixty mighty men stood on earth as the number above, and the Holy One took them from the lower world as He took the Patriarchs to be a holy chariot. A Tosefta tells how those two came to be here at all: when Adam was driven out they said that on earth they would have been righteous — can you master the evil inclination? we can — and He cast them down at once; once down, the inclination entered them, they took wives of all they chose, and were uprooted from their holiness.

R. Yeisa asked after זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת אָדָם, and R. Abba called it a supernal secret. Three books are opened on Rosh Hashana: the upper, from which everything and all writing goes out; the middle, the sum of above and below, the first Adam and the Written Torah; and the book of the generations of Adam, of the wholly righteous — the Tzadik, who makes generations. Then all was set right above and below in one pattern, male and female taken into one; and מִגְדַּל עֹז שֵׁם יְיָ is that same book, the tower being David’s.

A book was brought down to the first Adam, and by it he knew supernal wisdom; it reached the wise of the generation, and whoever merits to look in it knows that wisdom. Going out of the Garden he held it, and it flew from him; he prayed and wept, and it was given back, that wisdom not be forgotten from men. Chanoch’s book is from the same place. He is the youth, taken from the earth — a thousand keys in his hand, a hundred blessings taken daily and bound for his Master — and when the Holy One took him for His service He showed him the upper treasures and the Tree of Life at the middle of the garden, its leaves and branches, all of which we see in his book.

לֹא יָדוֹן רוּחִי בָאָדָם לְעוֹלָם: the river that flows out brought a supernal spirit from the Tree of Life and poured it into the other tree, and spirits were drawn into men for long days, until evils rose and stood at the opening and the spirit withdrew. R. Elazar reads בְּשַׁגַּם as Moshe, who lights the moon, and the hundred and twenty years as a hint to him, by whose hand the Torah was given and life poured down from the Tree of Life — as it would have remained had Israel not sinned: חָרוּת עַל הַלֻּחֹת, freedom from the angel of death. He holds below and above, and so Moshe did not die but was gathered from the world and lights the moon, as the sun, gathered, enters and lights her. Read otherwise, the long drawing of the spirit into men turned it to flesh. Seth’s generations were righteous, then spread and would have wasted the world with spears and swords, until Noach set the order of the earth right, for at first they neither sowed nor reaped; and the Holy One will yet set world and spirit right, that days be long as the days of the tree and death be swallowed forever.

R. Shimon: when the Holy One made the world He engraved it in the secret of faith, above and below in one secret, making the lower world in the pattern of the upper, this standing against that, so all should be one — engraving the letters above and below and creating worlds with them. So too the first Adam: crowned with supernal crowns, made in the six sides to be complete in all, and in the supernal image, so that all who looked at it trembled. Then He brought him into the Garden, the angels surrounding him and making known the secrets of their Master, and from there he looked into all the supernal secrets.

Seven halls are above and seven below in their pattern — six alike and one hidden away — each holding a likeness of above and of below; in them was Adam’s dwelling, and after he was driven out they were set in order for the souls of the righteous. The first is sealed, and no eye rules over it but theirs: those who did not exchange their Master’s glory for another fear, אֵשֶׁת חַיִל עֲטֶרֶת בַּעְלָהּ, and not after the fear called אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים. Leaving this world the souls enter, each sitting as long as it needs, clothed in garments patterned on this world, and through that vessel seeing the supernal images.

There too stand the converts, in a garment of light that shines and does not shine, in a place ringed with precious stone and gold; one opening goes down facing the opening of Gehinnom, where they see those who never entered the covenant driven by the angels of destruction in the burning fire, and they rejoice that they converted — and above them Ovadiah and Onkelos. The second hall lies within the first, near the Cave of the Patriarchs, and shines more: there stand those who bore sickness to be set right and never neglected their prayer, and innermost those who answer אָמֵן יְהֵא שְׁמֵיהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ with all their strength, for whom the light of all colours shines — and above them Mashiach. From there he goes into the third, where are those of greater pain, the schoolchildren who did not complete their days, and those who wept over the ruin of the Temple, and he comforts them; and into the fourth, the mourners of Zion and Jerusalem and those killed by the nations — and he begins, and weeps.
I:39-40:
All the princes of David’s seed hold to him and comfort him, and he weeps a second time until a voice goes out and rises and stays above until the new moon. Coming down it brings lights, and healing to the slain and the sick who bore pain with Mashiach. Then he puts on a purple robe, and in it are engraved all the slain of the nations; the robe rises and is engraved in the King’s own purple, and the Holy One will wear it to judge them — יָדִין בַּגּוֹיִם מָלֵא גְוִיּוֹת.

Within, at a higher grade, stand the ten appointed ones, R. Akiva and his fellows, who rise into the mirror above: of them it is written עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתְךָ. The fifth hall holds those of whole repentance, whose souls went out in purity, and those who sanctified the Name and took death upon themselves; at its gate stands Menashe, whom the Holy One received, digging him a tunnel to take him in. Further within are those of fierce repentance, whose souls went out in the hour of their bitterness — and each is scorched by the light of his fellow’s canopy.

The sixth is the hall of the chasidim, the hall of the right, above all the rest. None stands in it but they, and all who love their Master with a great love; at its door stand those who declare His oneness each day, and they rise first. Above that door is Avraham, the right hand of the Holy One; at another Yitzchak, bound on the altar; and within, Yaakov whole, the twelve tribes about him and the Shechinah over their heads. When Israel are in distress the three Patriarchs wake, and wake her to shield them.

The seventh is hidden and sealed from all the rest. In its middle stands a pillar of many colours — green, white, red, black — and a soul rising enters and goes up by the colour that is his. Six halls are for dwelling in and the seventh is not; and the six are in the secret of שֵׁת, which is why it is written בָּרָא שִׁית — six grades above and six below, one secret.

R. Yehuda on בְּרֵאשִׁית: two houses, the first Temple and the second, one above and one below; two ה’s, and all of them one. The upper ב opens gates to every side, each taken into the other. R. Yitzchak in R. Elazar’s name: it is the whole of the forms gathered in one — הוּא מַרְאֵה דְּמוּת כְּבוֹד יְיָ, the vision in which six others are seen: bara shit. R. Yosei on הַנִּצָּנִים נִרְאוּ בָאָרֶץ: those six are Avraham, Yitzchak, Yaakov, Yachin, Boaz and Yosef, seen in the land — and עֵת הַזָּמִיר הִגִּיעַ, the hour of praise.

R. Abba: the upper world is sealed and all its words sealed, and when it created it brought out these six. Being sealed, Scripture says it created six supernal days and does not say who; afterwards it uncovers the lower work and does — בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים, a name in the open. Hidden above, revealed below, so that His work is always both, and the secret of the Holy Name with it. אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם takes in the heavens below, וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ the earth with all her works, patterned above.

וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ is the upper earth, which has no light of her own: she was, precisely — she had been as she should be, and afterwards made herself small, and her light small. Tohu, bohu, darkness and spirit are the four elements. Read otherwise it is the earth below, made in seven dwellings after the pattern above — Eretz, Adamah, Gei, Neshiyah, Tziyah, Arka and Tevel, the greatest, וְהוּא יִשְׁפֹּט תֵּבֵל בְּצֶדֶק. Tziyah is Gehinnom’s place, the darkness on the face of the deep the angel of death’s; Tohu is Neshiyah, where no form appears until all is forgotten, Bohu is Arka, and the hovering spirit answers to Tevel, which is fed from it.

Seven dwellings above, grade upon grade, and seven below, all held one to another. The first is dark and does not shine, set for spirits and storms unseen: no light, no darkness, no form at all, with Tahariel over it and seventy officers who flare and are wiped away and renewed each morning. The second is lighter though dark, for the angels appointed over men’s deeds, to turn them aside on the road they walk; they feed on the scent from below, and Kedumiel is over them: they open in song and fall silent, unseen, until Israel below say theirs — then they stand and shine the brighter. The third is sparks and smoke, where the river of fire flows, the burning-place of the wicked’s souls, and Samael is found there.

The fourth is a place of light, for the angels of the right: they open in song and finish it and are not consumed, unlike the earlier ones, who are burned in the flame and return renewed. These are the angels of mercy, who never change — עֹשֶׂה מַלְאָכָיו רוּחוֹת — and Pedael is over them, holding the keys of mercy for those who turn back. The fifth shines more than all before it, holding angels of fire and of water, at times mercy and at times judgment, some singing at midnight and some at first light, with Kedushiel over them. When the night divides and the north wind stirs and the Holy One comes to delight with the righteous in the Garden, the wind strikes and they sing; at morning the rest sing, and the stars with them — בְּרָן יַחַד כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר — until Israel take up the song after them.

The sixth is the upper dwelling, near the kingdom of heaven: ships and rivers parted from the sea, fish swarming to the four sides, Uriel over all. The ships sail by hours and moments, each quarter with its angel — Michael east from the right, Gavriel north from the left, Refael south, Uriel west and last. Above them stands the seventh, where none is found but the souls of the righteous, delighted in that supernal radiance among the treasuries of peace and blessing. So too the earth below in its seven, all giving thanks, though none knows His glory as those of the highest do. And this world does not stand except for the righteous, who are holy bodies.
I:41-42:
As the seventh dwelling above is only for the souls of the righteous, so the seventh below is only for their bodies, that all should be one and each after the pattern of the other. R. Shimon: within those dwellings are seven halls of the secrets of faith, against the seven upper firmaments, each with its spirits. In the first, Rachmiel, over the souls of converts, who takes them and gladdens them with the radiance above.

In the second, Ahinael, over the souls of children who did not merit to labour in Torah: he stands over them and teaches them. In the third, Adrahinael, over those who meant to turn back and died before they had; driven in Gehinnom and then given into his hand, they long for their Master’s radiance and are not gladdened. These are called children of flesh: יָבוֹא כָל בָּשָׂר לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֹת לְפָנַי. In the fourth, Gadriel, over the souls of those slain by the nations, to bring them into the King’s purple, where they are inscribed until the day He avenges them. In the fifth, Adiriel, with Michael the great prince over them — and there the souls of the chasidim are delighted in the light that flows from the World to Come.

R. Shimon: who knows how to order his prayer before his Master as Moshe did, at length when length is called for and short when short? I have found in the books of the ancients an ordering of the secret of secrets in a single knot — to order a prayer, tie its knots, and unify a whole unification: to split firmaments and open gates, with none to hold his hand. Happy are the righteous, who know how to entreat their Master, annul decrees, settle the Shechinah in the world and take judgments away.

He rose and said: מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת יְיָ — who will clear the dust from your eyes, Avraham the chasid, right hand of the Holy One, to whom the secret was uncovered, who began prayer in the world and to whom the King’s halls were shown. Seven holy halls stand at their gates, and into each enters the prayer of one who knows how to please his Master and unify wholly, going into them all and tying knot to knot, spirit in spirit, lower in upper: יְיָ בַּצַּר פְּקָדוּךָ צָקוּן לַחַשׁ.

Of the first it is written וְתַחַת רַגְלָיו כְּמַעֲשֵׂה לִבְנַת הַסַּפִּיר. Here is a spirit called Sapphire, one light rising and descending and flashing white to every side, hidden and revealed at once; four lights part from it and all are one, as the lights of a burning lamp go and return and are one flame. To the left is a spirit called Levanah, taken into the first, red and white together since it comes out of those first lights; when its lights arrive they are taken in and the first alone are seen — וְלֹא נוֹדַע כִּי בָאוּ אֶל קִרְבֶּנָה.

From those two the holy Ofanim were made, whose law is the law of the Chayot; and the fire walking among the Chayot is that holy spirit they came out of, which gives them light. When spirit is taken into spirit a light goes out, one Chayah over four Ofanim, its form a lion, ruling thirteen hundred myriads of others: four wheels to each and three supports to a wheel. Each has four faces looking to the four sides of the Chayah above, and travelling they interlock as the loops set one against her sister, and a sweet voice is heard in the hosts below. Beneath this hall the forces spread through the lower firmaments as far as the star Shabbatai, all looking to it and fed from it. This is the hall called Livnat HaSappir.

Its light is never still, like the sun’s fire in water, and none stands over it but the will of a righteous man in the prayer that enters and rises to tie its knots. Then the light wraps itself in that prayer and rises with it into the knot of the second hall, the Chayah and the Ofanim with it, held one in another as fire in water and water in fire. In the middle of the hall a pillar is fixed, rising to the middle of the next and bored through from below upward so that spirit may cleave to spirit, and so to the top of them all: וְרוּחַ אֶחָד לַכֹּל.

Of the second it is written וּכְעֶצֶם הַשָּׁמַיִם לָטֹהַר: the spirit called Zohar, always white, its colours never mixed, a substance that never changes. It does not glitter openly; it is hard to bring out, like the white of the eye, which shines when the eye turns, and cannot shine at all until the lower takes hold and turns it. Then it takes another light to the left and turns with it: חַמּוּקֵי יְרֵכַיִךְ כְּמוֹ חֲלָאִים מַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵי אָמָּן. Happy is he who knows how to turn lights. White is tied to white, blue to the red below on the left, and together they are called Etzem HaShamayim, because everything beneath is taken up into them.

Out of those lights the Serafim of six wings were made, all in six because all are from Etzem HaShamayim — and whoever reads and repeats the six orders of the Mishnah is the one who knows how to tie the knot of his Master’s unity. When the lights turn, a Chayah goes out over four Chayot, and by them the serpents below are subdued, that came from the serpent which brought death to the world. When they travel, hosts tremble: some shine, some are broken and burned and renewed, and all hide beneath her wings. Four wheels look each to its quarter with three supports apiece, twelve travelling from a centre that opens and closes, and at every turning a voice is heard in all the firmaments.

So the spirit blazes and rises, to be tied by the will of a righteous man in the prayer he prays: entering that hall it takes all of them with it, joined one in another — fire in water and water in fire, spirit in earth and earth in spirit, east in west and north in south — until they reach the star Tzedek. And when it enters the third hall and is joined there within the pillar that stands in the middle, all is complete thus far, one spirit including all: וְרוּחַ אֶחָד לָהֵנָּה. Here is the bowing, to cleave to one’s Master.

The third is the hall of the spirit called Nogah, purer than all the rest: no colour is seen in it, neither white nor green nor black nor red, and so it is called tohar. Yet for all its purity it is not seen until the lower ones turn and take hold of it and enter; then its light shows, and it is none of their colours. Completed from all below, it brings out a light holding three, two of which rise and descend and glitter — and in that glittering twenty-two lights appear, each differing from the rest and all one. It shines only when the lower lights rise and the will of the prayer takes them all: then the two are seen as the number of the twenty-two letters of the Torah, and return and are gathered in. And this spirit does not settle in its own hall, but longs to rise into the fourth.
I:43-44:
The forms of the lion and the eagle are taken together and made one form in her. Beneath her stand four upper Ofanim like the colour of tarshish, each of eight wings, all coming out of the light that rules them. They stand to the four sides, four faces to each: two looking toward her, two covering with their wings against the flashing lights they cannot look at. Whenever they travel, out of their own sweat hosts are made that praise and are never silent, beyond number.

Four doors has this hall, ten appointed at each; and when the halls below rise in the will of a pure prayer they all open and are interlocked — Ofanim in Chayot, lights in lights, spirit in spirit. In it is a place like glittering gold where hosts are stored that do not rise until the knots are tied and the hall goes up to be crowned; then they come out filled with judgment, called the masters of shields, with golden shields hanging on every side, and they wage war with swords and spears against the messengers of judgment as far as the star Ma’adim. Then the hall rises crowned, and that place stays where it is, and is called the chamber of the runners.

When the prayer rises it takes these lights and hosts and ties their knots until spirit is tied in spirit and they are one, and they go into the pillar to be taken up in the fourth hall. Each needs the other, completed from below first and from above after. Whoever knows these secrets and makes that wholeness cleaves to his Master and annuls hard decrees; he crowns his Master and draws blessing on the world, and is the man called a righteous one, pillar of the world, whose prayer does not come back empty.

All of them need one another, and they are as the colours of the eye: what is seen when the eye turns, and what is not seen in that turning is the spirit that rules them all — for were there no colours, the hidden one over them could not be held at all. So everything hangs and is tied one to another. When all is taken up in the third hall and the will of the prayer rises to be crowned in the fourth, then all is one will and one knot. Here is the bowing, to be found acceptable by one’s Master.

The fourth is unlike them all: four halls one within another, and all of them one. Here is the spirit called Zechut, where the merit of every man is turned over. Seventy lights come out of it, standing in a circle and not spreading as the others do, joined and lighting one another; before them stand all the merits of the world, with two lights weighed as one. Facing them are seventy princes outside, going round the four halls, while the seventy and the two are innermost of all: בִּטְנֵךְ עֲרֵמַת חִטִּים סוּגָה בַּשּׁוֹשַׁנִּים.

Before those lights every deed comes to be judged. The two are the witnesses, for there are seven eyes of the Lord that range over all the earth, and whatever is done is inscribed in that very deed; the two see it and testify before the seventy, who decree for good or for ill. This is the place of merit. In that spirit three letters are inscribed — יה״ו — cleaving there as male and female cleave, never removed; and a light goes out shining to four sides which brings out three others, three courts judging the rest of a man’s matters: wealth and poverty, sickness and wholeness.

The spirit rises and brings out a blazing Chayah with eyes like a man’s, to watch over the masters of judgment, who take their notes and open and close in the world and finish the judgment. Beneath her four blazing Serafim with seventy-two wheels to each; when they travel a river of fire is made, and hosts that come singing from beneath the second hall give battle here and are burned. Every appointed one set to rule takes his rule from here, and from here it is taken from him and he is judged in that fire. All judgments go out from this hall, for good or ill — save three: children, life and sustenance, which are given no authority here, since they hang on that supernal river from which all lights flow.

Twelve doors, and at each the heralds who proclaim below whatever judgments are to come down — קָרֵא בְחַיִל וְכֵן אָמַר גֹּדּוּ אִילָנָא. The winged ones carry the word to the firmament of the sun, and when the sun comes out it goes with it to the serpent of the firmament in whose midst the stars are fixed; from there it spreads, until even the spirits and the birds of the sky make it known, and the heralds turn back and close the doors. A man on his sickbed is judged here for life or for death — life hangs above, and if he is judged here for life they give it from above. Here is the falling on the face, to overcome judgment: אֵל אֱמוּנָה וְאֵין עָוֶל.

The fifth is the hall of the shining lightning, a spirit that opens and closes and glitters to every side. From its glitter a light shines like purple, holding every colour — white and black, red and green, woven together until one embroidered Chayah is made whose form is a man’s, holding all forms. Out of her come four supports, one called Ofan which is two, for when the one appears the other shines within it: כַּאֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה הָאוֹפַן בְּתוֹךְ הָאוֹפָן. From the blazing spirit beside it two lights shine that are four, turning in their colours — and here is לַהַט הַחֶרֶב הַמִּתְהַפֶּכֶת, the turning sword, which stands over the seventy lights of the court: whence every judge who judges has a sword hanging over his head.

Those lights of the left brought out another Chayah over four that do not stand in their standing; when her spirit enters them two blazing sparks flash outward and turn continually — now female, now male, now spirits, now holy watchers. For out of that joining a spark goes out that blazes always and is never quenched, and runs after the two: they do their errand in the world and go out before they finish, and it strikes them and they are renewed — since it holds all four colours, and so they turn into each.

This spirit is taken into another, and here the two are seen as two and not as one, as those before them were: they stand in love, holding all that is below — שְׁנֵי שָׁדַיִךְ כִּשְׁנֵי עֳפָרִים תְּאוֹמֵי צְבִיָּה. And when two spirits spread into one another in love, this hall is called the Hall of Love, which stands always in its standing, hidden in the secret of secrets for whoever must cleave to it: אֶתֵּן אֶת דֹּדַי לָךְ. Then hosts come out beyond number — mandrakes, vines, pomegranates — as far as the star called Nogah, all in a love never parted. Here is the bowing and the spreading of hands, to cleave in love to one’s Master.

The sixth holds the spirit called the scarlet thread — כְּחוּט הַשָּׁנִי שִׂפְתוֹתַיִךְ — and is called the Hall of Will: the spirit that is the will all the lower spirits run after, to cleave to it with a kiss. Held in six and standing in six, it brings out twelve lights that rejoice to rise and to receive all beneath them. Whoever ties the knots and raises them here draws out will from the Lord in love. In this hall Moshe was gathered, in the love of one who kisses the kisses of love: it is Moshe’s hall, the spirit of love and of unity. From the glitter of the twelve come four holy Chayot of love, the great with which the small are joined, held to four sides as a nut is — which is why it is called the nut garden, אֶל גִּנַּת אֱגוֹז יָרַדְתִּי. The four part into twelve, three to a side, and all below are held in them until they are one; and then this spirit rises to be crowned in the spirit above called Shamayim, and once all below are tied to it, it says יִשָּׁקֵנִי מִנְּשִׁיקוֹת פִּיהוּ.
I:5-6:
A word of Torah newly said rises and is crowned, and out of it the Holy One makes new heavens and a new earth. The verse is read for its tense: אֲשֶׁר אֲנִי עוֹשֶׂה — not made, makes, continually, out of the renewals of Torah. R. Eleazar asks what וּבְצֵל יָדִי כִּסִּיתִיךָ means, and is told: when the Torah was given, myriads of angels came to burn Moshe with the flame of their mouths, until the Holy One covered him. And “to say to Zion, you are My people” is read עִמִּי אָתָּה, you are with Me — a partner: as I made heaven and earth by speech, so do you.

The other side of that is said at once, and sharply. One who has no business in the secrets of the Torah and renews words he does not properly know — that word goes up and is met by אִישׁ תַּהְפּוּכוֹת לְשׁוֹן שָׁקֶר, who leaps out of the great deep five hundred parasangs and flies six thousand in a firmament of falsehood; and the woman of harlotry comes out and joins him there, and from that place goes out and kills. R. Shimon asks the companions plainly: do not let a word of Torah out of your mouths that you have not known and heard properly from a great tree, so as not to be the cause of that killing.

With the Torah the world was made. He looked into her once, and twice, and three times and four, and then spoke, and then did — which is the four of אָז רָאָהּ וַיְסַפְּרָהּ הֱכִינָהּ וְגַם חֲקָרָהּ; and before the work itself four words go in, בְּ’רֵאשִׁית בָּ’רָא אֱ’לֹהִים אֶ’ת.

Then the road. R. Eleazar and R. Abba are travelling, and a man is driving donkeys behind them. R. Eleazar opens on אֶת שַׁבְּתוֹתַי תִּשְׁמוֹרוּ: each of the six days showed its work and was given its power on the fourth, since fire and water and air, upper elements though they are, all hang until the earth discloses them. And all of them hang on the Shabbat, which is the fourth leg of the Throne. Why two Shabbatot? Because the eve and the day are not two things.

The donkey-driver asks what וּמִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ is, will not take the answer, and opens himself. אֶת takes in the Shabbat boundary, two thousand cubits each way; שַׁבְּתוֹתַי is the upper Shabbat and the lower, two folded into one. And a third was left unnamed and stood ashamed, and said: Master of the world, from the day You made me I am called Shabbat, and a day is not without its night. She is answered, daughter, you are Shabbat and Shabbat I call you — but I crown you with a higher crown. And וּמִקְדָּשִׁי תִּירָאוּ is the point that stands in the middle, to be feared above everything, whose penalty is death.

They ask him who gave him leave to speak so, driving donkeys. He tells them of the Yod who came to him alone, kissed him and wept and said: my son, what shall I do for you? — but I am going up, and I shall be filled with many good things and hidden precious letters, and afterwards I will come to you and support you and give you an inheritance. And of his father, who dwelt in the great sea and was a fish that circled it from side to side, ancient of days, who swallowed all the other fish and then brought them out alive and full of every good. R. Eleazar looks at him and sees it: you are the son of the holy lamp, the son of Rav Hamnuna Saba, the son of the light of the Torah — and you are walking behind us with donkeys. They wept together and kissed him, and he opened on וּבְנָיָהוּ בֶּן יְהוֹיָדָע, and on מְקַבְצִאֵל, the hidden supernal rung that eye has not seen, in which everything is gathered.
I:7-8:
The elder finishes — the sun and the moon are never parted, and it is the moon's own praises that draw the sun to dwell with her — and the two fall before him, and when they look up he is gone. They search, and sit and weep. At last R. Abba says it: when the righteous walk a road with words of Torah between them, the worthy of that world come to meet them. It was Rav Hamnuna Saba, and he went before they knew him. They rose to load the donkeys and the donkeys would not move; to this day the place is called דּוּךְ דְּחַמְרֵי, the station of the donkeys.

R. Eleazar opens on מָה רַב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִירֵאֶיךָ — not “Your goodness” but the abundance of it: the light of the first day, hidden for the righteous; פָּעַלְתָּ the upper Garden and נֶגֶד בְּנֵי אָדָם the lower, where the souls bathe in dews of rivers of pure balsam — and are sometimes seen before men, to work wonders as the supernal angels do, as we have just seen a supernal lamp and were not worthy to look longer. R. Abba answers from Manoach, מוֹת נָמוּת כִּי אֱלֹהִים רָאִינוּ: he said it because no man sees and lives, and we have seen and were sustained.

They come to a mountain as the sun goes down, and the branches of its trees strike one another and sing. A voice: sons of God, holy ones scattered among the living of this world, lamps of the academy, gather to your places to delight with your Master in the Torah. And again: mighty rocks, high hammers — the Master of colours stands upon the pillar; enter and gather. Then the branches themselves, קוֹל יְיָ שׁוֹבֵר אֲרָזִים, and they fell on their faces and came down out of the mountain in haste.

R. Shimon tells them before they can tell him: I was sleeping and saw you, and Benayahu ben Yehoyada sending you two crowns by the hand of an elder — a sage is greater than a prophet, says R. Yose. Then he wept over יְיָ שָׁמַעְתִּי שִׁמְעֲךָ יָרֵאתִי, Chavakuk's verse: he is the Shunammite's son, called from אַתְּ חוֹבֶקֶת בֵּן, and there were two embracings, his mother's and Elisha's — the alphabet his father engraved in him flew from him at his death, and in the embrace Elisha engraved the two hundred and sixteen letters of the seventy-two Names, by which his body stood again. And he wept once more that Rav Hamnuna Saba had been seen face to face by them and not by him; then saw him uprooting mountains and lighting lamps in the palace of the King Messiah. From that day he called his son and R. Abba פְּנִיאֵל.

R. Chiya opens on רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת יְיָ. It should say the end of wisdom; it says beginning because fear is the way in. The King made gates upon gates and at the end of them one gate with many locks: whoever does not enter by it never enters at all. ב is two points joined, one hidden and one revealed, and because they do not part they are called רֵאשִׁית, one and not two. It is the fear of the Lord because it is the tree of good and evil — merit, and it is good; do not, and it is evil — while שֵׂכֶל טוֹב is the tree of life, with no evil in it. And לְכָל עוֹשֵׂיהֶם are those who uphold the Torah: whoever labours in her has no doing while he labours, and the doing belongs to those who support him.

R. Shimon was labouring in the Torah on the night the Bride is joined to her Husband. The companions of her palace are needed that night — to be with her and rejoice in her adornments, from Torah to Prophets to Writings and the secrets of wisdom, for these are her ornaments. She comes in with her maidens and stands over their heads all that night, and the next day does not enter the canopy but with them. Whoever sets her adornments in order this night is written in the book of remembrance and blessed with seventy blessings of the upper world.

He opened on הַשָּׁמַיִם מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד אֵל: the Bridegroom entering the canopy, shining with the brightness of sapphire from one end of the world to the other; and כְּבוֹד אֵל the Bride, called אֵל all the year and now כָּבוֹד as well. Every companion who made her ready is named there — וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו מַגִּיד הָרָקִיעַ, the work of His hands being those who keep the covenant sealed in the flesh. On which Rav Hamnuna Saba said אַל תִּתֵּן אֶת פִּיךָ לַחֲטִיא אֶת בְּשָׂרֶךָ: they draw such a man to Gehinnom, whose appointed one is דּוּמָה — who has no permission over those who kept the covenant.

Which brings the trial of David. Dumah claimed him; the Holy One answered that Bathsheba was appointed to him from the day the world was made, that none went out to war without freeing his wife by a bill, and that Uriah never came near her — My Name sealed in his own for testimony, אוּרִיָּה and אוּרִיָּהוּ. And the months were counted out: not three but four, from the proclamation on the twenty-fifth of Nisan to the Day of Atonement and גַּם יְיָ הֶעֱבִיר חַטָּאתְךָ לֹא תָמוּת — which is, not by Dumah's hand. One claim was left: David had opened his own mouth and said חַי יְיָ כִּי בֶן מָוֶת הָאִישׁ הָעוֹשֶׂה זֹאת, passing sentence on himself. You have no permission, said the Holy One — he confessed before Me though he had not sinned. Dumah went back crestfallen, and David said כִּמְעַט שָׁכְנָה דוּמָה נַפְשִׁי: a thread's thickness, the measure standing between him and the other side. A man must guard himself from such a word, for he cannot plead before Dumah that it was an error, as David could.
I:9-10:
The psalm is finished: out of those words the firmaments were made, and לַשֶּׁמֶשׁ שָׂם אֹהֶל בָּהֶם — the holy sun sets his dwelling in them and is crowned by them, and then כְּחָתָן יֹצֵא מֵחֻפָּתוֹ, running through them; מִקְצֵה הַשָּׁמַיִם מוֹצָאוֹ, out of the upper world, and תְּקוּפָתוֹ the circuit of the year turning to every side, and nothing hidden from him in the hour he grows warm and turns back in whole longing. All that praise is for the Torah's sake, תּוֹרַת יְיָ תְּמִימָה — six times the Name, six verses, and בְּרֵאשִׁית six letters, בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ six words.

R. Eleazar and R. Abba come in, and R. Shimon says the faces of the Shechinah are coming. וְהוּא הִכָּה אֶת הָאִישׁ הַמִּצְרִי אִישׁ מִדָּה חָמֵשׁ בָּאַמָּה — a man of measure is Shabbat and boundary, and a man of measure in the plain sense, his length from one end of the world to the other as Adam's was; and the spear in his hand, כִּמְנוֹר אֹרְגִים, is the staff of God, cut with the explicit Name in the letter-combinations Betzalel engraved — the weaver — shining that Name on every side in forty-two colours. Sit, precious ones, and let us renew the Bride's adornment this night: whoever joins with her is guarded above and below and comes through the year in peace.

R. Shimon opens בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים. Whoever says there is another god is destroyed from the worlds — אֱלָהַיָּא דִּי שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְקָא לָא עֲבַדוּ יֵאבַדוּ, a verse set in Aramaic but for its last word, so that the holy angels, who are also called אֱלֹהִים and who did not make heaven and earth, should not take it as said of them and be jealous of a man.

And אַרְקָא rather than אַרְעָא, because Arka is one of the seven lower earths, where the children of Cain went down when he was driven from the face of the ground — a doubled earth, folded out of darkness and light. Two appointed ones rule it, עַפְרִירָא and קַסְטִימוֹן, in the shape of angels with six wings, one like an ox and one like an eagle, and joined they make the shape of a man; in the darkness they turn into a two-headed serpent and fly into the deep, and when they reach the chain of Uzza and Azael they wake them. At night they go to Naamah, mother of demons, who leaps sixty thousand parasangs and takes many shapes so that men should stray after her; and they rove the world and rouse the children of Cain with a spirit of evil desire. Their heavens are not these heavens, and יֵאבַדוּ is said of this upper earth — that they should not rule in it, or bring men to defilement.

R. Eleazar asks what praise lies in מִי לֹא יִרָאֲךָ מֶלֶךְ הַגּוֹיִם. It comes to shut the mouth of those who think their thoughts are unknown. A philosopher once put it to me: you say none among the wise of the nations is like Him — but among the wise of Israel there may be, as no prophet arose in Israel like Moshe though one arose among the nations. You have spoken well, I told him. Who revives the dead but the Holy One — and Eliyahu and Elisha revived them. Who brings rain — and Eliyahu withheld it and brought it. Who leads the sun — and Yehoshua silenced it. He decrees and the righteous of Israel annul it, צַדִּיק מוֹשֵׁל יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים — and He commanded them to walk in His ways, to be like Him in everything. The philosopher went and became a Jew in Kfar Shechalayim and was called Yose Ketina, and learned much Torah.

Then the verse itself. Everywhere He wished to be praised in Israel and is called only upon Israel; the nations said, we have another patron in heaven. So the verse says מֶלֶךְ הַגּוֹיִם — to subdue them; the wise of the nations are the great ones appointed over them, and their kingdoms the four that rule above at His will, and none of them can do the smallest thing but as He commands. Who among them could make as You make? The work of the holy King is heaven and earth; of their kingdom it is written וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ.

Let each of you set one adornment on the Bride, said R. Shimon; and to his son, give her a gift. R. Eleazar opened on מִי זֹאת עֹלָה מִן הַמִּדְבָּר: מִי and זֹאת are two holinesses of two worlds joined in one bond, so that she may be a holy of holies; and מִן הַמִּדְבָּר is also מִן הַדִּבּוּר — for the plagues struck Egypt בַּמִּדְבָּר in settled land, which means by speech. By the word of the mouth she rises between the wings of the Mother, and by speech comes down and rests on the heads of the holy people.

How does she rise by speech? From the first word of the morning. The early pious ones set a vessel of water beside them and washed when they woke in the night, and rose and laboured in Torah — for the cock crows at exactly midnight, and then the Holy One is found with the righteous in the Garden of Eden, and one may not bless with defiled hands. When a man sleeps his spirit goes out and an unclean spirit rests on his hands; and by day too he may not bless or read one word until he washes — not because they are dirty, for with what are they dirtied? There is a spirit in every privy in the world that takes its pleasure in that filth, and at once it rests on a man's fingers.

And whoever rejoices on the festivals and does not give the Holy One His portion — which is to gladden the poor as far as he is able — the Satan accuses him and takes him from the world. For on those days the Holy One comes to look at His broken vessels and sees they have nothing to rejoice with, and weeps, and goes up to destroy the world; and when the academy pleads His mercy He answers, did I not make the world on kindness alone, אָמַרְתִּי עוֹלָם חֶסֶד יִבָּנֶה? Who was greater than Avraham, who did kindness to every creature? Yet at every feast of joy the accuser comes to see whether the poor were served first: if they are in the house he departs, and if not he goes in and accuses. So when Avraham called the great of the generation to the feast of Yitzchak, the accuser stood at the door in the likeness of a poor man and none looked at him — for Avraham was serving those kings, and Sarah was nursing their children before them, since they would not believe she had borne a son.
III:210-211: The close of Balak. Why did the Holy One open the mouth of Balaam’s ass? So that this master of enchantments should learn that speech was never his: a dumb beast speaks when it is given words, and so does he. Balak’s seven altars are read through a parable — a gift prepared for the king and handed instead to the dogs; the offerings were fit, the intent was not, and what was meant to rise was thrown below. Even the verse that meets him is marked: וַיִּקָּר, “and He chanced upon him” — a word of uncleanness, and of uprooting — not the וַיִּקְרָא of love with which Moshe was called. Balaam is left a mouthpiece for כֹּה, the grade from which both blessing and curse issue; but כֹּה was long since promised to Israel — כֹּה יִהְיֶה זַרְעֶךָ — so his mouth could only bless. From the top of the rocks he sees the fathers, from the hills the mothers, a people rooted where no curse reaches. “Who can count the dust of Jacob” — even their dust is beyond number. “Behold, the people riseth up as a lioness” — rising in the morning like lions to seize tzitzit, tefillin and Shema. The three blessings answer the three blows he struck the ass. At the last his one weapon is the evil eye, and against it: “the spirit of God was upon him” — spread over Israel as a mother spreads her scarf over her child’s head, so that no eye can rule over them.
III:212-213: Balak’s close, and Pinchas opened. Did the holy spirit ever rest on Balaam? R. Eleazar says it did not: “the spirit of God was upon him” means upon Israel — spread over them as a man spreads his scarf over a child’s head in the street, so that no evil eye can reach it. Balaam, who had an evil eye like no other, turned his face toward the wilderness — toward the calf they had made there — hunting an opening; and finding none he did what the evil eye always does first, and praised. “How goodly are thy tents” is the admiration of a man who takes hold of another’s beautiful hands only to wish them in his own box; and “water shall flow מִדָּלְיָו” he read as from his poor — let the shoot of Torah come only from the poor among them. But the veil of holiness was over them. Israel crouched and lay down as a lion, and a lion over its prey cannot be moved: even among the nations, even lying down, they hold to the ways of Torah, and no king of the world uproots them. Balaam had forged Egypt’s fetters himself and thought them unbreakable — and God brought Israel out. So he went back to his people: tearing his flesh and pulling out his hair, he climbed to the mountains of darkness, where Azael the open-eyed and Uzza sit among flaming beasts, and a man must throw the ashes of a white cock into the face of the small creature that meets him, strike the chain to the abyss three times, and come kneeling with his eyes shut; fifty days they teach him. He returned with no way to harm Israel, and gave Balak the counsel of the women instead. Only then was the end of days shown to the power that rules enchantment, and spoken through him: a star of seventy streamers rising on the sixth day, the twenty-fifth of the sixth month, burning seventy days; three walls of Rome fallen on the first of them; wars in every quarter and no faith among men; the Land shaken forty-five miles around the place of the Temple; from the opened cave a branch that rules the world, and the King Messiah — and Israel going out in joy, the Shechinah going out with them. Pinchas begins on his zeal: unqualified for greatness, he was raised to it and given the priesthood in perpetuity, though a priest who kills is disqualified — the י added to his name as the ה was added to Yosef, both for guarding the same covenant. The wholly righteous builds on his own inheritance, digs his own wells, plants his own trees; the other raises a fair house on a crooked foundation. And the covenant of peace given him is peace from the Angel of Death: he did not die as other men die, but departed in celestial yearning.
